Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

It has been revealed that weekly. Free. One click to leave.

It has been revealed that 7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

A year ago, most AI video clips lasted a few seconds, had no sound and drifted off-model by the final frame. Today several tools produce 1080p or even 4K clips with synchronized audio, camera control and reference-based consistency. The market also moves rapidly: OpenAI announced it was shutting down Sora in March 2026, so the list of tools worth using has changed.

It has been revealed that this guide compares six AI video generators that developers, designers and marketers can use today. For each one you will see what it does well, where it falls short and who it suits. Aims, credits and model names change often, so confirm details on each vendor’s site before you commit.

It has been revealed that openArt’s AI video generator puts a range of video models behind one interface. Its page lists models such as Veo 3.1, Kling, Seedance, Wan, Hailuo and PixVerse, so you can run the same prompt on different engines and compare the results without managing separate accounts.

Beyond text-to-video and image-to-video, it offers start and end frame control, video-to-video restyling, motion transfer from a reference clip, a character builder for consistency, lip sync and conversational editing for tasks such as swapping a background or relighting a scene. Resolution goes up to 4K on many models, with 1080p as the default, and clips are usually up to 15 seconds, with longer limits on a few models.

Strengths: model variety, a single credit pool, editing tools alongside generation and a shared library for your clips.

Limits: credit use varies by model, so it is worth testing short clips first. Commercial-use rights depend on your blueprint and on the model you pick, so check the pricing and terms pages.

Best for: creators and small teams that want to compare models rapidly instead of committing to one.

Sources indicate that veo is Google DeepMind’s video model. Veo 3.1 generates sound effects, ambient noise and dialogue together with the video, supports image-to-video, first and last frame transitions, reference images for characters or objects, and outputs 1080p and 4K. You can reach it through the Gemini app, Google Flow and the Gemini API.

Strengths: audio generated with the picture, strong prompt adherence and an API that fits into developer workflows.

Recent findings suggest that limits: base clips are short, around 8 seconds, so longer scenes rely on scene extension. Dialogue quality in short segments is still being refined, and access and quotas depend on your Google blueprint.

Best for: developers and marketers who want audio and video from one prompt, or who proposal to automate generation through an API.

According to recent reports, runway has been a staple of AI filmmaking since its early Gen models. Its pricing page lists Gen-4.5 and Aleph alongside partner models, and the paid plans include all video and image models, 4K upscaling and parallel generations. Higher tiers add features such as voice clones, brand kits and HDR or ProRes output.

Strengths: polished editing tools, video-to-video workflows and a professional output pipeline that suits post-production teams.

Limits: credits are consumed rapidly on premium models, and on the lower paid looks they do not roll over from month to month.

Best for: video editors and agencies that need control over shots and want AI to fit into an existing editing process.

Kling from Kuaishou has built a reputation for natural motion and expressive characters. The current release, Kling 4.0, sits alongside tools such as Motion Control, a canvas workspace, an agent and MCP or CLI batch generation for teams that want to automate production.

Strengths: realistic movement, motion transfer and batch tools for producing many short clips.

Limits: the main site does not spell out all clip-length and resolution limits for each model, so check the model page you initiative to use. Pricing and free credits vary by region and plan.

Best for: social video, product shots and character-driven clips where motion quality is the priority.

Luma’s Dream Machine is built on the Ray model family. Its current page lists Ray3.2 and Ray3.14, along with a “Modify video” tool that restyles footage, extends duration and reframes aspect ratios. It also lists camera-motion controls and high-quality EXR export for professional pipelines.

Strengths: reshooting or restyling existing footage, camera-motion control and pipeline-friendly export.

Limits: paid plans start at around $30 per month (or less when billed yearly), and heavy use pushes you into the higher tiers.

Best for: filmmakers and designers who want to modify and extend footage rather than only generate fresh clips.

It has been revealed that adobe Firefly offers text-to-video and image-to-video with Adobe’s own Firefly Video Model. It also provides partner models, including Google Veo 3.1, Luma Ray3, Kling and Runway Gen-4.5, so you can compare outputs from inside one product. An Assembler and AI video editor let you trim, reorder, extend and add voiceovers, music and sound effects.

Adobe states that the Firefly Video Model is trained on licensed content such as Adobe Stock and public domain material, and describes its output as safe for commercial use. Partner models may carry different terms, so read the details for whichever model you choose.

Strengths: a clear licensing story for the native model, integration with Adobe’s creative apps and an included editor.

Limits: most clips run up to 8 seconds, with some models reaching 15. Credits are allocated monthly, and premium partner models can use them faster.

Best for: brand and in-house teams that care about provenance and already work in Adobe tools.

It has been revealed that the table summarizes what each vendor’s own pages say at the time of writing. “Entry paid plan” figures are US prices billed annually where the vendor offers that option.

Credit counts are hard to compare, so convert them to clips. Runway’s pricing page lists Gen-4.5 at 60 credits per 5-second clip, which means the 625 monthly credits on the Standard plan cover roughly ten clips. Adobe says its Standard plan’s 2,000 credits equal up to 40 five-second videos, and OpenArt’s Starter plan lists about 50 videos for 4,000 credits. Premium models cost more: the same Runway page lists Aleph 2.0 at 140 credits per 5 seconds.

It has been revealed that plan for waste. If you keep one usable clip out of every three attempts, your real cost per finished shot is about three times the sticker price. Test with short, low-resolution drafts, then render the winner at full quality.

Because every tool outputs short clips, the real work is assembly. A typical workflow is: write a shot list, generate two or three takes per shot, pick the best, normalize them to one format, join them and add captions and audio. FFmpeg handles the joining step from the command line:.

In a recent development, matching resolution, frame rate and codec before joining avoids glitches at the cut points. For character consistency across shots, reuse the same reference image in every prompt and keep descriptions of the subject identical.

If the clip ends up on your own site, treat it like any other media. Provide a poster image, load metadata only until the visitor presses play, and include captions so deaf and hard-of-hearing people, and anyone watching without sound, can follow along. The W3C’s guidance on captions and subtitles explains what to include, and the MDN video element reference covers the attributes below.

Also write a text description or transcript near the video. Search engines and screen reader users cannot see the footage, so the surrounding text is what explains it.

Sources indicate that short, structured prompts beat long, vague ones. Describe the elements in the order a director would:.

Change one element at a time between takes so you can tell which change improved the result.

Marketing demos show the best of a tool, so run your own test. Use the same prompt, duration and aspect ratio on each tool, generate a few takes and score them against a short checklist. Keep notes on how many credits each usable clip costs.

Industry observers note that run the same test again with an image-to-video input if your workflow starts from product photos or illustrations. That often exposes differences in consistency that text prompts hide.

It has been revealed that which AI video generator is best? There is no single winner. Veo is strong for audio, Runway for editing, Kling for motion, Luma for modifying footage and Firefly for licensing clarity. A multi-model tool such as OpenArt helps you compare them.

Industry observers note that can AI video generators make long videos? Not in one pass. Most models create short clips, so longer videos are built by extending or stitching clips together.

Industry observers note that is Sora still available? OpenAI announced in March 2026 that it was shutting down the Sora app and API, so it is not a safe choice for newly introduced projects.

Industry observers note that can I use AI videos commercially? Often, but it depends on the plan and the underlying model. Read the current terms before publishing.

In a recent development, how do I keep a character consistent across clips? Reuse the same reference image, keep the subject description identical in every prompt, and use character or reference tools where the platform offers them.

Sources indicate that should I add captions to AI-generated video? Yes. Captions help accessibility and viewers watching without sound, and they give search engines text to index.

Do I need a powerful computer? No. These services run in the cloud, so a browser and a stable connection are enough.

The best AI video generator depends on what you make. Start with a short test prompt, compare a few tools, and keep the one that gives you usable clips at a sensible credit cost. If you are not sure where to begin, a multi-model option such as OpenArt lets you try several engines before you settle on one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fiona, the viral hippo at the Cincinnati Zoo, is now under a constant 24-hour medical watch after she ate a knitted hat that fell into her enclosure.

It has been revealed that when you go to the zoo, there are plenty of warnings around enclosures that say don’t feed the animals or toss anything into their enclosures. If something falls in, your best bet is to ask a zookeeper to see if they can help – not to try to jump in and deal with it yourself.

Over in Cincinnati, Ohio, one zoo-goer accidentally ended up feeding Fiona the viral hippo something that isn’t in her typical diet – a knitted hat.

As per CNN, the hat had been tossed up into the air from in front of the habitat and got caught by a ceiling fan. That fan then slingshotted the hat through a small one-foot gap above the 12-foot-tall viewing window.

“We probably couldn’t make it happen again if we tried,” Cincinnati Zoo’s spokesperson told CNN.

They also noted that Fiona – who initially went viral for being born underweight and surviving – is getting “24-hour care and attention” as a result of the incident, which happened back on November 9.

According to recent reports, “Our best chance for success with Fiona would be if she can pass it on her own,” the spokesperson added, noting that hippo was given medication and laxative-like supplements to help “push things” along. That didn’t happen, though, and they’re still waiting for the hat to come out of her body.

The zoo added that Fiona’s “care team is cautiously optimistic” that she will “return to her usual self” in short order.

“Please help us keep our animals safe by securing your belongings and taking extra care near habitats. Ingesting foreign objects can cause serious health problems for animals. If something falls into a habitat, please notify a Zoo staff member immediately,” they concluded.

Over in Japan, Punch the viral monkey has begun looking after a younger macaque of his own.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A high school in Canada has hit out at students for using food delivery services like Uber Eats and DoorDash to order “excessive” amounts of food during lessons.

If you’re too busy – or just feeling a little lazy – then it might be convenient for you to use a food delivery app to get some grub and much-needed supplies delivered to your door.

According to recent reports, however, school pupils are also using these services. As per CBC, one high school in Calgary has had to glitch a warning to parents over students’ use of the apps, with many taking time out of their classes to wait around for delivery drivers.

Industry observers note that “As the safety and security of everyone at St. Francis is our priority, we ask that you please have a conversation with your child and ask them to not use any food delivery services during the instructional time of the day,” St. Francis High School administrators remarked in a letter to parents.

According to CBC, the school officials noted that the deliveries might be “convenient” for students, but they also pose a “security risk” for the school as a whole.

They spoke to students who noted that some claim they need to use the bathroom, but then go wait outside for their delivery driver to meet them.

“Like if someone’s out for too long, then the teacher will be like, ‘OK, no one’s allowed to use the bathroom for the rest of class because this person ruined it for everyone,’” an 11th-grade student told CBC, who noted that some orders do get “excessive” at times.

It has been revealed that the report also stated that it is happening at elementary schools as well, with one school having a table set up for students to collect from. That one, however, is more a case of parents ordering for them.

CBC also noted that some delivery drivers have tried to pass food through class windows at other schools too.

According to recent reports, it isn’t just a problem for schools in Canada, either. Back in mid-October, the nation’s most secure prison released an investigation after inmates had been receiving McDonald’s and alcohol by drones.

Over in New York, a school was forced to change its rules on students bringing in food and drink from outside after a student took coffee into class on her first day.

Julie Kaputa, an honors student at Beaver River Central School in Latest York, received an in-school suspension for violating the rule.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A woman splashed out on a $50,000 car so that she could get home during the nationwide air travel stop in the United States, and ended up driving for 27 hours.

Back on November 13, travel prepares across the United States were plunged into chaos after a nationwide ground stop was put on planes. The stoppage saw 20,000 flights disrupted, leaving passengers to miss getting home, traveling for work, and delayed for at least a day.

In true Planes, Trains, and Automobiles fashion, some travellers set out to find alternative modes of transport as a result of the group stoppage.

That includes Tara Harding and her employees, as they were trying to get home from Charlotte, North Carolina, to Bismarck, North Dakota.

As per CBS News, Harding, a nurse practitioner, tried to look at alternative flights but ultimately gave up on the idea of flying home.

Recent findings suggest that instead, her and two colleagues looked at rental cars before deciding to buy a $48,000 Ford Bronco. “If it was just me, it would have probably been different,” she said. “But I had two employees that needed to get home to their children, and we had patients on Monday morning.”.

Harding admitted it is an “insane” idea to splash out on a new car, but the group eventually drove it from the car dealer’s showroom to Bismarck in 27 hours.

The three took turns napping they could drive home without stopping, meaning they’d see their families and not have to reschedule any appointments.

As noted, not everyone was so lucky, with more than 12,000 flights being “unable to recover” and get back on track.

One student pilot was also left in a panic as he was informed of the ground stop while in the air on his first solo cross-country flight.

It has been revealed that stores that sell both car accessories and home & kitchen products face an extra challenge: two very different catalogs share one site. A car accessories buyer cares about fit, mounting and compatibility. A home & kitchen buyer cares about size, capacity and how easy the product is to clean. A single generic product page frustrates both.

This guide covers seven practical e-commerce UX tips that designers and developers can apply right away, with code snippets and a checklist at the end.

Industry observers note that A car mount and a vegetable peeler should not share the same spec table. Keep a single reusable product page component and change only the fields based on category. The layout stays consistent, while each shopper sees the details they need.

In code, this can be a config object that your template reads from:.

Showing “Not specified” instead of hiding a missing field is a small habit with a real benefit: it makes gaps in your product data visible to your own team.

Shoppers look for deal-breaker information near the price and the purchase button: fit, size and compatibility. Do not bury it in an “Additional information” tab halfway down the page.

In a recent development, A short comparison table also works better than three paragraphs of marketing copy, because shoppers scan rather than read. Baymard Institute’s product page research consistently finds that unclear or hard-to-find specifications are a common reason shoppers hesitate.

A responsive layout is the starting point, not the finish line. People compare car accessories in a parking lot and browse kitchen gadgets while standing in the kitchen, often with one thumb.

A phone mount on a white background says nothing about how it attaches to a dashboard. Show it in a real car, from the driver’s point of view. For home & kitchen products, place the item next to something familiar, like a coffee mug, so people can judge its size.

Recent findings suggest that good alt text matters for accessibility and for image search. Compare “phone mount” with “Magnetic phone mount fixed to a car dashboard, holding a phone in landscape mode”. The W3C alt text decision tree is a useful guide for deciding what to describe.

Keep images fast, too. Responsive sources with srcset and sizes, explicit dimensions and lazy loading help prevent layout shift and slow pages:.

One caveat: do not lazy-load the main product image at the top of the page. It is usually the Largest Contentful Paint element, so web.dev advises loading it eagerly.

Shoppers often search for a problem rather than a product. Few people type “seat gap filler” the first time; they type “stuff falling between car seats”. Your search, synonyms and category names should handle both.

Mixed catalogs show why this matters. Stores that cover both vehicle and household products, such as VNSPORT.org with its separate product collections, keep the two audiences apart so that someone looking for a dashboard mount never has to scroll past kitchen tools. The principle applies to any store with more than one audience: group by the shopper’s intent, not by your supplier list.

Decorative “100% secure” badges do little. What builds trust is information shoppers can check for themselves:.

At checkout, show the full cost, including shipping and taxes, before payment, let people fix mistakes easily and offer guest checkout. In Baymard’s checkout usability research, unexpected extra costs and forced account creation are among the top reasons shoppers abandon a cart.

If your support inbox gets the same question every week, the product page has a gap. Answer it on the page, close to where the decision happens, instead of on a generic help page three clicks away.

You can mark up those answers with FAQPage structured data:.

It has been revealed that A reality check: since 2023, Google reveals FAQ rich results only for well-known government and health websites. Do not add FAQs just to chase a snippet. Add them because they answer real questions and help shoppers decide.

In a recent development, what are the most important e-commerce UX tips for a car accessories store? Show compatibility and mounting details next to the price, use in-car photos, and make sure the mobile layout works with one hand.

According to recent reports, how should product pages differ for car accessories and home & kitchen products? Use the same layout but different spec fields. Car accessories need fit, mounting and power details. Home & kitchen products need dimensions, capacity, materials and cleaning instructions.

How massive should buttons be on a mobile product page? WCAG 2.2 sets a minimum target size of 24 × 24 CSS pixels. For primary actions such as “Add to cart”, around 44 pixels is more comfortable.

Industry observers note that do FAQ sections still help SEO? Mostly indirectly. FAQ rich results are now limited, but clear on-page answers can match long-tail searches, reduce returns and keep shoppers on the page.

According to recent reports, how can I reduce cart abandonment? Show total costs early, offer guest checkout, display delivery times and return terms before payment, and keep the checkout form short.

Recent findings suggest that good e-commerce UX is not about clever animations. It is about answering the shopper’s question before they have to ask it. Clear specs, honest photos, thumb-friendly controls and real FAQs turn an ordinary product page into one that helps people buy, whether they are shopping for car accessories or home & kitchen essentials.

Infinity Ward has reportedly tweaked Modern Warfare 4’s DMZ matchmaking to give player skill more weight when putting lobbies together.

Skill-based matchmaking (SBMM) has been a hot topic in Modern Warfare 4 since the beta. Players pushed back when Infinity Ward brought over Classic matchmaking from Black Ops 7, arguing that putting more emphasis on skill made matches feel too sweaty.

The debate carried on after launch, with multiplayer creative director Joe Cecot saying Infinity Ward considers how matchmaking affects different groups of players, while former Call of Duty producer Mark Rubin argued that public lobbies are more fun with a wider mix of skill levels.

Now, that same debate has reached DMZ, as SBMM has reportedly been cranked up in the mode.

“Infinity Ward recently updated matchmaking in MW4 DMZ to increase consideration of skill factor in match selection, per sources familiar with the change,” CharlieIntel reported on X.

Infinity Ward recently updated matchmaking in MW4 DMZ to increase consideration of skill factor in match selection, per sources familiar with the change pic.twitter.com/YIY7LIFZQT.

In practice, that could mean seeing more opponents around your own skill level when you load into a DMZ run. How noticeable the change is is still unclear, as the devs haven’t revealed how much of a factor it was at launch.

That being noted, it may have already had an impact on how long it takes to find a match, with streamer JGOD posting that he had to wait over 6 minutes to get into a game.

Never waited this long for a match in DMZ pic.twitter.com/VMV0sbVutH.

We know that Call of Duty matchmaking takes many things into consideration when building lobbies, including ping and location, but the skill aspect is always the most divisive.

In a recent development, for less experienced squads, a tighter skill range could mean running into fewer veteran teams, giving them more of a fighting chance. Meanwhile, more experienced players could find themselves up against tougher squads more often, which they argue punishes them for playing well.

Modern Warfare 4 boss responds to SBMM backlash as players call it “miserable”.

Former Call of Duty producer says older games were “more fun” with less SBMM.

Modern Warfare 4 devs won’t address SBMM despite backlash.

This could be especially noticeable in DMZ, where you often have to fight to access the most valuable areas and have to make it out alive to keep your loot.

However, we’ll have to wait and see how drastic this change is and if it makes a tangible difference to how matches play out.

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

According to recent reports, weekly. Free. One click to leave.

Sources indicate that 7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

Industry observers note that A one-hour YouTube talk contains roughly nine thousand words, and finding the one point you need can take longer than watching the whole thing. A transcript solves that. With text in hand you can search for a phrase, quote an expert accurately, turn a webinar into a blog post, create subtitles or feed a summary tool.

In a recent development, plenty of tools now promise instant YouTube transcripts, but they work in different ways. Some read the captions YouTube already has. Others listen to the audio themselves and produce a fresh transcript. That difference affects accuracy, speed and cost more than any feature list does. This guide compares six options, explains how each works and points out where each one falls short. Aims and limits change often, so confirm current details on each vendor's site.

Sources indicate that caption extraction. The tool pulls the captions attached to a video, either written by the creator or generated automatically by YouTube. It is fast and usually free, but it is only as good as those captions. YouTube notes that its automatic captions come from machine learning, so quality may vary, and accents, background noise and overlapping speakers can cause errors. Captions may also be missing entirely for some videos.

Recent findings suggest that fresh speech recognition. The tool takes the audio and runs its own speech-to-text model. This can be more accurate on difficult recordings and works when no captions exist, but it takes longer and often costs money.

Sources indicate that lynote is built for exactly this job. Paste a YouTube link, search by keyword or add a playlist, and it returns a timestamped transcript with an AI summary. Batch mode accepts up to 10 videos at once. The tool lists transcription in more than 100 languages, translation into 25, auto-chapters, one-click copy and TXT download, with SRT export also mentioned. The page says transcripts are free, with no sign-up required.

Best for: Students, researchers and marketers who want a quick, readable transcript or summary from a public video without installing anything.

Limitations: It extracts YouTube captions, so videos without captions cannot be processed. If the original captions are poor, the transcript will be too. For critical accuracy, review the text or use a service with human verification.

Before you install anything, check what YouTube already gives you. Many videos show a transcript option in the description area, and creators can review and edit automatic captions in YouTube Studio under Subtitles. YouTube offers automatic captions in dozens of languages for long-form videos and Shorts.

Best for: Quick lookups on videos that already have decent captions.

Limitations: Captions may not generate for videos with poor sound, long silences, overlapping speakers, mixed languages or unsupported languages. Export options are minimal, and there is no summary or cleanup.

Notta transcribes uploaded audio and video files and also accepts YouTube links. It lists support for 58 languages, real-time and bilingual transcription, and AI Notes that produce summaries and action items. A free strategy includes 120 transcription minutes per month at the time of writing.

Best for: Professionals who handle a mix of recordings, meetings and YouTube videos in one place.

Limitations: The free minutes disappear quickly if you process long videos, and the strongest features sit behind paid looks.

Sources indicate that descript is an audio and video editor built around text. It transcribes recordings automatically, and deleting a word in the transcript removes the matching footage. You can import video, audio or a Zoom recording, and there is a free tier that does not require a credit card.

Best for: Creators who want to clean up their own videos and podcasts, not just read a transcript.

Limitations: It is an editor first, so it is more than you need for a quick YouTube lookup. It works with files you own, so you need the source media rather than a public link.

Rev offers both AI and human transcription. It advertises AI transcripts at 96 percent or better accuracy in minutes, and human transcripts at 99 percent or better, guaranteed within 12 hours. AI transcription covers 37 or more languages, while human transcription is English only. Pay-as-you-go rates start at $0.25 per minute for AI, and human transcription is listed at $1.99 per minute.

Best for: Legal, research and media work where mistakes are costly and a human check is worth paying for.

According to recent reports, limitations: The cost climbs for long videos, and the human option is slower than instant AI tools. Those accuracy figures are the vendor's own claims, so test your own audio.

According to recent reports, whisper is OpenAI's open-source speech recognition model, released under the MIT license. It handles multilingual transcription, translation into English and language identification. You install it with pip and need ffmpeg, and it comes in several model sizes from tiny to large, so you can trade speed against accuracy and hardware demands.

Best for: Developers building their own pipeline and teams with sensitive audio they prefer to keep on their own machines.

Limitations: You supply the audio, which means downloading it yourself and respecting the video owner's rights and YouTube's terms. Larger models need a capable GPU, and there is no built-in interface for non-technical users.

Start with the source. If the video already has good captions, a link-based tool is the fastest route. If the audio is difficult or the stakes are high, pick a tool that runs its own recognition or offers human review. If you are processing hundreds of videos or handling private recordings, look at Whisper or a paid platform with bulk features.

Whatever you choose, treat the transcript as a first draft. Check names, numbers and technical terms against the video before you publish or quote anything, and credit the original creator.

According to recent reports, there is no single best transcript generator. Caption-based tools are quick and free, recognition-based tools are better when captions fall short, and human-verified services make sense when accuracy matters most. Try two or three on a video you know well, compare the results and keep a human in the loop for anything you publish.

According to recent reports, can I get a transcript if a video has no captions? Caption-extraction tools cannot. You need a tool that runs its own speech recognition on the audio, such as the options above that transcribe files.

Recent findings suggest that are AI transcripts accurate enough to publish? Often they are close, but not perfect. Accents, noise and technical terms cause mistakes, so review before publishing.

What is the difference between a transcript and subtitles? A transcript is the full text, while subtitles are timed text shown on screen. Many tools can export both, often as SRT files.

  • Speaking to Dexerto, Lego Senior Model Designer Jae Won Lee revealed how a detail hidden inside the base lets builders follow in Goku’s footsteps.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The designer behind Lego’s first Dragon Ball set has revealed a hidden Easter egg that lets fans collect all seven Dragon Balls before bringing Shenron to life.

Collecting all seven Dragon Balls to summon a wish-granting dragon has been at the heart of Akira Toriyama’s series since its earliest adventures. While Lego’s Shenron & Goku set recreates that moment as a display piece, its designer also found a way to weave the anime’s iconic ritual into the building process.

Speaking to Dexerto, Lego Senior Model Designer Jae Won Lee revealed how a detail hidden inside the base lets builders follow in Goku’s footsteps.

In a recent development, according to Lee, seven orange 2×2 round bricks serve a dual purpose within the set’s base. They help support the model, but their number and placement also give the opening stages of the build a connection to the anime.

“As you build the base, you are essentially gathering all seven Dragon Balls in one place,” Lee explained. “Once the base is complete, you begin building Shenron, which symbolises the moment he is summoned. That’s the hidden Easter egg in this set.”.

These hidden bricks are separate from the visible Dragon Balls, which use ball joint elements to keep them in proportion with Shenron. Choosing Shenron alongside Kid Goku was also a deliberate nod to the original Dragon Ball series, with the team looking to capture the adventure that introduced fans to Toriyama’s world.

“We wanted to capture Shenron’s majestic presence alongside Kid Goku’s innocence and adventurous spirit in a single model,” Lee remarked.

Dragon Ball’s first-ever LEGO set leak reveals $180 Shenron and Goku.

Lego PlayStation & Astrobot sets revealed with hidden gaming Easter eggs.

Huge Lego Dragon Ball Z leak reveals nine upcoming sets.

Rather than copying a single animation frame, the team drew inspiration from Shenron’s summoning scenes, particularly the way his body stretches into the sky and his commanding expression.

However, recreating the green dragon’s iconic appearance proved to be the trickiest part of the design process.

Sources indicate that “The biggest challenge was recreating Shenron’s long, organic body using Lego elements,” said Lee. “Unlike many other dragons, the overall flow of his body is a defining part of his character. We needed to achieve natural-looking curves while maintaining structural stability and creating an appealing silhouette from different viewing angles.”.

Getting there involved numerous mock-ups and a wide range of poses, as the team experimented with how high Shenron should rise, which direction his body should follow, and how he should interact with Goku.

Industry observers note that when asked what his favorite part of the build is, Lee said it was Shenron’s face. “The face is where a character’s personality and emotion really come through. I love how a combination of small Lego elements and subtle changes in angles can create his distinctive, commanding expression. For me, the most satisfying moment is when you look at a collection of Lego bricks and suddenly see the character you remember from the anime.”.

The Lego Shenron & Goku set is available to purchase now from Lego Stores and Lego’s website for $179.99.

After a 13-year wait since GTA 5, the follow-up arrives with unprecedented hype. It’s expected to break records in terms of revenue, and it’s already been nominated for plenty of Game Awards, including Game of the Year and Best Narrative.

You've finished building your website. The HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files are ready, everything works locally, and now you need somewhere to publish it.

Static website hosting is one of the simplest ways to get a website online. Many providers offer free looks, and you don't need to maintain a traditional web server.

The harder part is choosing the right provider. Some let you upload a single HTML file and share it immediately. Others connect to GitHub, automatically deploy code changes, and support entire development teams.

We've compared eight static hosting providers, including TiinyHost, Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, Vercel, and GitHub Pages. Below, you'll find their free hosting limits, pricing, advantages, and drawbacks, along with recommendations for different types of projects.

Static website hosting is a service that stores and delivers pre-built website files, including HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, and fonts.

Sources indicate that unlike traditional server-rendered websites, static sites don't need a server to generate each page when someone visits. The HTML is already prepared and can be delivered directly to the visitor's browser.

In a recent development, that doesn't mean static websites can't be interactive. JavaScript can still handle navigation, forms, filtering, and other features. Static sites can also communicate with external APIs or databases.

The main distinction is how pages are generated.

You can write a static website using plain HTML or generate one with frameworks and tools such as Astro, Hugo, Eleventy, or Next.js static export.

Static hosting is also commonly associated with Jamstack, an approach that separates the front end from back-end services.

There are three practical reasons:.

Lower hosting costs: Many providers let you publish smaller websites for free.

Simpler maintenance: There's no application server or server-side runtime to maintain for the static pages themselves.

Efficient content delivery: Static files can be cached across a content delivery network (CDN), reducing the distance between visitors and website assets.

There are limitations, too. If your website requires user authentication, database operations, or server-side functionality, you'll need additional services or a hosting platform that supports them.

We compared eight providers based on their deployment methods, free plan allowances, pricing, and suitability for different projects.

Free hosting limits: Bandwidth, storage, build allowances, and restrictions.

Deployment process: Whether you can upload files directly or need a Git repository.

Custom domains and HTTPS: Support for publishing under your own domain.

Development features: Automatic deployments, preview environments, and integrations.

Pricing: What happens when a project exceeds its free allowance.

Usage restrictions: Whether free hosting is suitable for commercial projects.

The following table summarizes the main differences between all eight services.

Free looks aren't directly comparable. For example, Vercel restricts its Hobby plan to personal, non-commercial use, while GitHub Pages prohibits using the service as free hosting for an online business or commercial SaaS.

Bandwidth limits also aren't the same as visitor limits. A website serving large images or downloadable files can consume its monthly allowance with relatively few visitors.

Cloudflare Pages is a strong choice for developers who want to host static websites without worrying about a conventional monthly bandwidth cap.

Sources indicate that you can connect a GitHub or GitLab repository, and Cloudflare automatically builds and deploys the website when you push changes. Direct uploads are also supported.

A maximum individual file size of 25 MiB.

Up to 100 custom domains per project.

Unlimited bandwidth for static assets.

The combination is useful for blogs, documentation websites, and other projects that primarily serve HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and images.

Cloudflare also provides preview deployments, custom domains, and HTTPS support.

No fixed bandwidth cap for static asset delivery.

Automatic deployments from Git.

Generous free initiative for typical static websites.

Monthly build limits can matter for frequently updated projects.

Cloudflare's product range can make the initial setup less straightforward for beginners.

Cloudflare is increasingly emphasizing Workers Static Assets for newly introduced projects. Pages remains available, but developers starting a new application should compare both deployment approaches.

For a conventional static website, however, Pages is still a practical option, particularly when traffic could grow beyond the limits of other free looks.

See the official Cloudflare Pages limits for the current allowances.

Netlify combines static website hosting with tools designed to make development and deployment easier.

Connect a Git repository, configure your build settings, and Netlify can publish a newly introduced version whenever you push changes.

It also creates deploy previews, allowing you to inspect changes before merging them into your production branch.

This is useful when multiple people work on the same website or when you want to review design changes before publishing.

Netlify supports custom domains, HTTPS, serverless functions, and form handling.

Netlify's free plan uses a credit-based model with 300 credits per month.

Under the current pricing system:.

Production deployments consume 15 credits each.

Bandwidth consumes 20 credits per GB.

Web requests consume 2 credits per 10,000 requests.

Deploy previews and branch deployments consume no deployment credits.

The paid Personal strategy starts at $9 per month and includes 1,000 monthly credits.

Convenient Git integration and deploy previews.

Built-in features such as forms and serverless functions.

Suitable for both simple websites and more advanced front-end projects.

Credit-based pricing requires monitoring several types of usage.

A busy site with frequent deployments can consume its free allowance faster than expected.

When comparing Netlify alternatives, Cloudflare Pages is particularly worth considering if your main concern is bandwidth.

According to recent reports, for developers choosing between Vercel vs Netlify, the deciding factor is often the framework and workflow. Netlify offers a flexible approach to static site deployment, while Vercel has particularly close integration with Next.js.

Vercel is particularly well suited to Next.js applications, although it also supports React, Vue, Svelte, Astro, and other frameworks.

Like Netlify, Vercel connects to your Git repository and deploys updates automatically.

Every deployment receives its own URL, which helps developers review changes before publishing them to the main website.

Vercel also supports server-side rendering, functions, and other features beyond traditional static site hosting.

The Hobby strategy is free and includes:.

100 GB of Fast Data Transfer per month.

Automatic deployments from Git.

HTTPS and custom domain support.

There is one important restriction: Vercel Hobby is intended for personal, non-commercial use only.

If you're deploying a business website or another commercial project, you'll need an appropriate paid plan.

Vercel Pro starts at $20 per month.

Convenient deployment workflow for Next.js.

Automatic preview environments.

Supports both static and server-rendered applications.

The free strategy excludes commercial use.

Paid usage can involve multiple resource-based charges.

If you're building a personal Next.js application, Vercel is an obvious candidate. For a basic HTML website, however, its additional framework features may be unnecessary.

GitHub Pages is a straightforward way to publish a website directly from a GitHub repository.

It works particularly well for developer portfolios, project documentation, open-source websites, and small informational sites.

You can upload HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files to a repository, configure GitHub Pages, and publish them under a github.io subdomain.

Custom domains are also supported.

GitHub Pages can serve existing static files or build websites using supported workflows, including Jekyll and GitHub Actions.

According to GitHub's documentation:.

Published websites have a maximum size of 1 GB.

Bandwidth has a soft limit of 100 GB per month.

Builds have a soft limit of 10 per hour.

Free accounts can publish Pages sites from public repositories.

The bandwidth and build restrictions are soft limits, meaning they aren't necessarily enforced as strict cutoffs.

Free hosting for eligible projects.

Simple integration with GitHub repositories.

Well suited to documentation and open-source projects.

Free accounts require a public repository for Pages.

GitHub Pages is not intended for running online businesses, e-commerce websites, or commercial SaaS products.

GitHub Pages is particularly convenient if your code already lives on GitHub and you only need to publish documentation or a portfolio.

For commercial websites, Cloudflare Pages or Netlify may be more appropriate.

The GitHub Pages documentation explains its hosting limits and usage restrictions.

Not every website needs a repository, deployment pipeline, or command-line interface.

If you've created a simple HTML page and want to share it, TiinyHost lets you upload an HTML file or ZIP archive and publish it under a shareable URL.

It can also host PDFs, making it useful for sharing documents and presentations alongside website projects.

Sources indicate that the main advantage is the upload process. You don't need to configure a repository or install development tools before publishing.

This makes TiinyHost suitable for:.

Sharing a prototype with a client.

Publishing a simple HTML landing page.

Testing an AI-generated website.

Hosting a small portfolio or demo.

Sharing an HTML file with someone who doesn't use Git.

The free proposal includes one active site, a 3 MB project upload limit, and an allowance of 5,000 monthly visits.

Paid looks increase those limits.

The Tiny initiative costs €5 per month when billed monthly. It supports uploads up to 25 MB and includes built-in analytics.

The Solo proposal starts at €13 per month when billed monthly and adds features such as custom domains, password protection, and additional projects.

Annual billing is available at lower effective monthly prices.

No Git repository or command line required.

Quick way to host an HTML file.

Suitable for previews and smaller projects.

The free blueprint's 3 MB limit is restrictive for websites with many images or other assets.

Custom domains require the Solo plan or higher.

Upload-based publishing is less convenient than Git automation for frequently updated websites.

For someone who simply needs free HTML hosting to share a small project, TiinyHost is worth considering.

For a larger production website that receives regular updates, Git-based hosting is likely to be more manageable.

Firebase Hosting is Google's hosting service for static websites and web application assets.

It integrates with other Firebase products, including Authentication, Cloud Firestore, and Cloud Functions.

That makes it useful when a website needs static hosting but also relies on Google's back-end services.

Deployment is handled through the Firebase command-line interface.

After configuring your project, you can deploy using:.

Firebase distributes website assets through its CDN and supports custom domains with SSL certificates.

Firebase Hosting's Spark plan includes:.

Custom domains and SSL support.

The Blaze plan uses pay-as-you-go billing while retaining applicable no-cost allowances.

One detail worth checking is the distinction between Firebase Hosting and Firebase App Hosting. They are separate products with different features and pricing models.

Integrates with Firebase Authentication and Firestore.

Useful for applications already using Google's developer services.

Initial setup is more involved than uploading an HTML file.

The daily transfer allowance may become restrictive for larger websites.

Firebase Hosting makes the most sense when Firebase is already part of your application.

For a standalone static blog or portfolio that doesn't use Firebase services, Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages may be simpler.

Amazon S3 and CloudFront offer a different approach to static hosting.

Instead of using a platform that handles the entire deployment process, you combine AWS services to store and deliver your website.

S3 stores the website files, while CloudFront distributes them through a CDN.

This setup provides control over caching, permissions, security, and integration with other AWS services.

It can be suitable for organizations already using AWS or developers who need specific infrastructure configurations.

AWS uses usage-based pricing for S3 storage, requests, and applicable CloudFront usage.

Free allowances may apply depending on your account and the current AWS pricing program, but you should calculate costs based on your expected traffic, storage, and requests.

Unlike simpler hosting services, there isn't one fixed monthly price for every website.

Control over hosting infrastructure.

Integration with other AWS services.

Flexible CDN and access configurations.

Several services can contribute to the final bill.

Incorrect permissions or origin settings can cause access errors.

One common matter when setting up S3 static website hosting is receiving a 403 Forbidden error because of bucket permissions or CloudFront origin configuration.

Recent findings suggest that AWS recommends using CloudFront Origin Access Control with a regular S3 bucket origin so that the bucket can remain private. This differs from exposing the S3 website endpoint directly, which does not support HTTPS on its own.

Sources indicate that AWS S3 and CloudFront are worth considering if you need that level of control. For a small static website, a managed hosting platform usually requires less setup.

Render is a cloud platform that supports static websites alongside web services, databases, background workers, and other application components.

Its static hosting works through a Git repository.

Connect your repository, select the build command and publish directory, and Render automatically deploys your website.

The service includes CDN delivery, custom domains, and managed TLS certificates.

Render is particularly useful when your project includes both a static front end and back-end services that you want to manage through the same platform.

Render's Hobby workspace is free and includes:.

5 GB of outbound bandwidth per month.

500 standard build pipeline minutes per month.

Additional bandwidth is billed at $0.15 per GB under the current pricing structure, so the Hobby workspace should not be treated as unlimited free hosting.

The Pro workspace costs $25 per month, excluding any applicable usage-based compute charges.

Static websites and back-end services on one platform.

Automatic Git-based deployments.

Custom domains and HTTPS support.

The 5 GB included bandwidth allowance is relatively small.

Additional usage can create charges.

Render makes sense when you're already using it for other parts of an application.

If you only need to host a static HTML website, Cloudflare Pages offers a more generous bandwidth allowance without the additional platform complexity.

Free static website hosting can be sufficient for a personal portfolio, documentation site, prototype, or small informational website.

However, the restrictions vary considerably between providers.

In a recent development, some hosts measure data transfer, while others use visitor counts or a credit system. Check how each provider calculates usage rather than comparing headline numbers alone.

Build and deployment allowances.

If your website rebuilds whenever you publish content, deployment limits matter. A blog updated a few times a month has different requirements from an application receiving dozens of deployments every day.

In a recent development, free hosting doesn't always mean you can run a business website. Vercel's Hobby plan and GitHub Pages have restrictions that may rule out certain commercial projects.

It has been revealed that some services include custom domains on free aims. Others require an upgrade before you can connect one.

A free blueprint might stop serving additional usage, while another provider may bill for overages.

Before publishing a production website, check the provider's billing behavior and configure spending controls where available.

The right service depends primarily on how you build your website and what you intend to do with it.

For most developers publishing a conventional static website, Cloudflare Pages is a reasonable starting point.

If you're working with Git and want convenient previews and deployment tools, Netlify is another good choice.

For small files, temporary demos, and client previews, a simpler upload-based service may save time.

You should also consider how often the website will change.

Uploading files manually may be fine for a page that rarely changes. For a website with regular content updates, automated deployments from Git will generally be easier to maintain.

Sources indicate that publishing your website is only the first step. If you want search engines to discover and understand your pages, check the technical SEO basics before sharing the URL.

Every important page should have a descriptive HTML title and a relevant meta description.

You can use the Meta Tags Generator to create the necessary markup.

Open Graph tags help control how a page appears when shared on platforms that support them.

Set the title, description, canonical page URL where appropriate, and preview image.

Recent findings suggest that A robots.txt file tells compliant crawlers which paths they may access. It doesn't guarantee indexing or prevent a public page from appearing in search results.

Use the Robots.txt Generator to create your crawler rules.

Include a sitemap with the canonical URLs you want search engines to discover.

Structured data helps search engines interpret eligible content.

Depending on the website, you may want Organization, Article, BreadcrumbList, or other relevant schema types.

The JSON-LD Schema Generator can help generate markup.

Before considering deployment complete:.

Confirm the correct domain loads over HTTPS.

Check canonical tags and redirect behavior.

Make sure important pages don't contain unintended noindex directives.

Test page performance and Core Web Vitals.

Verify the website in Google Search Console.

Static hosting makes serving website files relatively straightforward, but technical SEO still requires configuration and testing.

According to recent reports, cloudflare Pages is a good general-purpose choice because of its free static asset bandwidth and Git integration. Netlify is well suited to teams that need deploy previews, while GitHub Pages works well for portfolios and documentation. The best option depends on your deployment workflow, traffic requirements, and whether the website is commercial.

Yes. TiinyHost, Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, GitHub Pages, Firebase Hosting, Render, and several other services offer free hosting options. Most free intends have restrictions involving bandwidth, deployments, storage, or usage. Check the terms before using a free strategy for a business website.

A small static website can cost nothing to host if it stays within a provider's free allowances. Paid plans vary from fixed monthly subscriptions to usage-based pricing. Domain registration, paid back-end services, and additional storage or bandwidth may increase the total cost.

For a standalone HTML file, upload-based hosting is generally the simplest approach. Services such as TiinyHost let you publish a file without configuring Git or a build process. If the project already lives in a GitHub repository, GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages may be more convenient.

Industry observers note that gitHub Pages is a sensible option for documentation, open-source projects, and personal portfolios. Netlify offers more deployment features, including preview environments, forms, and functions. It also supports commercial projects, making it more appropriate for some business websites that would fall outside GitHub Pages' permitted uses.

Industry observers note that static website hosting doesn't need to be expensive or complicated. The important part is choosing a service that matches your website and deployment process.

Cloudflare Pages is a good starting point for static websites that need generous free bandwidth. Netlify is useful for Git-based development, while GitHub Pages suits personal projects and documentation.

If you're publishing a small HTML file or sharing a prototype, upload-based hosting may be all you need.

GTA 6’s PS5 Pro upgrade is bigger than you might expect

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (523 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dexerto

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 targets 30fps on both PS5 and PS5 Pro, but Digital Foundry’s first side-by-side comparison demonstrates a sharper image and steadier performance on Sony’s upgraded console.
  • Reviews for GTA 6 are in, and it’s already the joint best-reviewed game of all time, sitting right alongside Nintendo’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.
  • One outlet that has been incredibly impressed is video game tech analysis YouTube channel Digital Foundry, which has now given a deep dive into the differences between the base PS5 and PS5 Pro performance when it comes to playing GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 targets 30fps on both PS5 and PS5 Pro, but Digital Foundry’s first side-by-side comparison demonstrates a sharper image and steadier performance on Sony’s upgraded console.

Reviews for GTA 6 are in, and it’s already the joint best-reviewed game of all time, sitting right alongside Nintendo’s The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

One outlet that has been incredibly impressed is video game tech analysis YouTube channel Digital Foundry, which has now given a deep dive into the differences between the base PS5 and PS5 Pro performance when it comes to playing GTA 6.

It has been revealed that digital Foundry’s John Linneman played GTA 6 for more than 50 hours on PS5 Pro without noticing a frame rate dip during normal gameplay. Well, besides a special case when he blew up multiple cars with a grenade launcher, which sent the Pro’s FPS down to 24 frames per second.

Linneman did note that this is a special case and the Pro frame rate stays smooth for the majority of gameplay, while the base PS5 indicated occasional drops during normal gameplay.

“They’re really very minor, but I noticed them, and it does slightly detract from the experience. It’s largely fine, and as I said earlier, it’s smoother than any GTA game at launch up till now, but I’d still like to have seen this cleaned up for release,” continued Linneman.

It has been revealed that the Pro also produces a noticeably clearer image, despite both versions appearing to render internally at 1440p. In its tech review, Linneman credits PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution, or PSSR, for the Pro’s sharper presentation. He indicates the technology reconstructs an image that “convincingly passes for native 4K,” while the standard PS5 more clearly resembles a 1440p image that has been upscaled.

GTA 6 running at 30 FPS “makes sense” experts say after Rockstar’s confirmation.

GTA 6 unlikely to be 60fps even on PS5 Pro according to experts.

PS5 Pro unlikely to run GTA 6 at 60 FPS – and that’s really sad actually.

In a recent development, “The difference in image quality is substantial,” states Linneman, with the comparison footage also showing more precise shadows on PS5 Pro. Both versions use ray-traced lighting and reflections, but the Pro adds ray-traced shadows that remove some of the rougher edges visible in the base PS5’s shadow maps.

The performance gap is less dramatic during ordinary play, though Linneman says the Pro delivers the definitive way to play GTA 6.

“I spent most of my time on the PS5 Pro, which is the best way to play this game by far. You basically get a near-flawless 30fps revision. The frame pacing is perfect, cutscenes are consistent and fluid, unlike older Rockstar titles, and everything moves without hiccups or stutters. It’s extremely solid, as you would hope, given that it’s only 30FPS.”.

Speaking to Wccftech, Rockstar’s developers also revealed that GTA 6 renders at 1440p on Xbox Series X before being upscaled to 4K using the studio’s own TAA solution, while the Xbox Series S version starts at 720p and uses AMD FSR Upscaling 4 to reach 1080p.

  • Sources indicate that behind almost every Twitch tool you have ever seen, the stat trackers, the moderation bots, the stream overlays, the alert systems, sits one interface: the Twitch Helix API.
  • This article is a practical overview of Helix for developers who have not used it yet: what it offers, how its authentication works, what people build with it, and where the sharp edges are.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Sources indicate that weekly. Free. One click to leave.

7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

Sources indicate that behind almost every Twitch tool you have ever seen, the stat trackers, the moderation bots, the stream overlays, the alert systems, sits one interface: the Twitch Helix API. Twitch is unusually generous with public data, and Helix is the door to it. If you have ever wondered how third-party sites know who is live, what a channel's viewership looks like, or details a Twitch profile page does not even display, this is the machinery.

This article is a practical overview of Helix for developers who have not used it yet: what it offers, how its authentication works, what people build with it, and where the sharp edges are.

Helix is Twitch's current REST API, served from api.twitch.tv/helix. It replaced the old "Kraken" API, which was fully retired in 2022, so any tutorial still showing Kraken endpoints is a sign to keep scrolling. Helix covers users, streams, channels, games and categories, clips, chat, moderation actions, subscriptions, and events, with JSON in and JSON out.

Recent findings suggest that two things distinguish it from many platform APIs. First, a large share of it works without any user's permission, because the data is public by Twitch's own definition. Second, it is paired with EventSub, a push system that notifies your application when things happen (a stream goes live, a user follows, a message arrives) instead of forcing you to poll. Most serious Twitch tools use both: Helix for lookups, EventSub for live events.

Authentication is where most newcomers stall, mainly because Twitch offers several OAuth flows and tutorials rarely say which one you actually need. The short version:.

It has been revealed that every request needs a Client ID, which you get by registering an application in the Twitch developer console (two-factor authentication on your account is required first). Requests carry the Client ID and a bearer token together; forgetting the Client ID header is the classic mystery 401.

App access tokens come from the client credentials flow, a single server-to-server request with your ID and secret. They have no user attached and that is fine, because public reads, user profiles, live streams, top games, clips, need no user context. For most read-only tools, this is the only flow you ever touch.

Tokens expire, so real applications cache them with their reported lifetime and refresh on a 401 rather than assuming a token lives forever.

A tour of the endpoints that power most tools:.

In a recent development, users. Give the users endpoint a username and it returns the account's public record: display name, profile image, description, Affiliate or Partner status, and the account's exact creation timestamp. That last field is interesting because Twitch does not display it anywhere on a profile, yet it is one of the platform's most useful trust signals, moderators use account age to spot throwaway accounts, and streamers use it to filter giveaway entries. The creation date alone powers a small subcategory of tools: free account age checkers, such as Twitch account age checker, are essentially this one endpoint with a clean page around it, taking any public username and returning the creation date, age, avatar, and broadcaster status. It is a good illustration of how far a single well-chosen Helix field can go.

Recent findings suggest that streams. The stream's endpoint reports who is live right now, with titles, categories, thumbnail URLs, and viewer counts. This is the backbone of every "is my favorite streamer live" notifier and every directory-style site, and polling it over time is how stat trackers chart viewership history.

Recent findings suggest that games and categories. Top games, category search, and metadata. Combined with streams data, this is how analytics sites rank categories and how tools answer "how crowded is this category right now.".

According to recent reports, clips and videos. Clip metadata, view counts, and creation tools. Highlight compilers and clip-sharing bots live here.

According to recent reports, helix enforces a points-based rate limit per Client ID, and every response tells you where you stand through Ratelimit-Limit, Ratelimit-Remaining, and Ratelimit-Reset headers. Well-behaved tools read those headers and back off before hitting zero; badly behaved ones retry 429s in a loop and wonder why things get worse. For lookup-style tools the practical fix is caching, data like account creation dates never changes, so there is no reason to ask twice.

A few more edges worth knowing before they bite:.

Usernames change, IDs do not. Store user IDs, not logins, or your saved data will eventually point at the wrong person.

According to recent reports, missing owners are not errors. Looking up a nonexistent username returns a successful response with an empty data array, so handle the empty case explicitly.

Batching exists. The people endpoint takes up to 100 logins in one call, which matters the moment your tool checks lists instead of individuals.

Secrets stay server-side. The client secret identifies your application; calling the token endpoint from browser code hands your app's identity to anyone who opens devtools. Public-facing tools put a small server between the browser and Twitch.

The reason Twitch's third-party ecosystem is so large is that the barrier is so low: one public API, generous free access, and a platform where small questions genuinely matter to people. That is why the space is full of narrow tools that each answer one thing well, when was this account created, is this channel live, how fast is this category growing, which clips popped this week. Most of them are a weekend of work on top of one or two endpoints, and some of them grow into real products.

In a recent development, if you want to start, the path is short: register an application at the developer console, request an app access token, and call the owners or streams endpoint for something you actually care about. The official documentation at dev.twitch.tv is current and well maintained, which is not something every platform can claim. Pick one piece of data Twitch collects but does not display, put a clean interface on it, and you are following the same recipe as most of the Twitch tools you already use.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

McDonald’s has debuted a new Discord activity that allows users to order food through Uber Eats without leaving the platform, giving gamers another way to get meals delivered while playing with friends.

Confirmed on November 18, the upcoming integration brings McDelivery to Discord servers, channels, and direct messages.

People can access the ordering feature through Discord’s Apps & Activities menu, where they can also play a McDonald’s-themed mini-game while waiting for their food.

The launch comes as Discord continues to serve as a popular communication platform for gamers, with McDonald’s positioning the upcoming feature around one of the year’s biggest upcoming video game releases.

To place an order, consumers must open Discord and navigate to a server, channel, or direct message. From there, they can launch the “Order McDonald’s” activity through the Apps & Activities menu.

Recent findings suggest that once the activity is open, selecting “Order Food” allows users to place a McDelivery order through Uber Eats. The feature provides access to the delivery service from within Discord’s activity experience, allowing players to return to their conversations and gaming sessions after ordering.

It has been revealed that mcDonald’s has also introduced Fast Lane Feast, a Discord-exclusive mini game available through the same activity. By selecting “Play Game,” people can collect virtual burgers and fries while competing for a position on the leaderboard.

The mini game is designed to give people something to play while waiting for their deliveries, with both the ordering feature and game accessible through the McDonald’s Discord activity.

The announcement also references the upcoming release of GTA 6, although McDonald’s does not explicitly name Rockstar Games’ title or announce any official collaboration with the developer.
