LangSmith is closed-source and restricts self-hosting to enterprise licenses, teams that run their own LLMOps stack and want to keep traces on their own servers need an alternative. To find the best fit, we set a baseline by tracing a small TypeScript agent (equipped with two tools) in LangSmith Cloud. Then, we ran the exact same agent through Langfuse, Arize Phoenix, Opik, and AcruxCore using each platform's recommended TypeScript setup. All tests were run on November 5, 2026, and we pulled every trace back through each tool's API to verify the data.

Recent findings suggest that all four alternatives successfully recreated LangSmith’s trace tree for the test prompt: a single agent span containing three LLM calls and two tool calls. The real differences between them come down to how much boilerplate code you have to write, how spans are typed, whether costs are tracked, and the overall server footprint.

Why Teams Look for a LangSmith Alternative.

Industry observers note that langSmith remains the best choice if you already use LangChain and allow cloud hosting—it required just 25 lines of code in our test. The alternatives below are for teams that don't fit that profile.

To test these platforms, we built a simple customer support agent equipped with two tools:.

Both tools use static fixture data to ensure every test run is identical. The agent runs a standard loop: it prompts the model, executes any requested tools, and stops once the model provides a final answer.

We tested the agent with three specific prompts to see how the tracing handled different levels of complexity:.

For our comparison, we focused entirely on the third question because it generates a robust, multi-step trace.

Under the hood, the agent uses the standard openai package to call the qwen3.8-flash model. We originally picked this model based on its reliable tool-calling behavior during early probing thought it once skipped a tool call later.

In a recent development, we used LangSmith as our baseline. By tracing the agent there first, we created a checklist of every field it captured, and we judged all the alternatives against that exact list.

Recent findings suggest that for setup, we followed the recommended TypeScript approach from each tool's documentation. Phoenix didn't have specific instructions for using its register() helper with OpenAI in TypeScript, so we adapted the pattern from their Anthropic guide.

All five SDKs shared one package.json.

According to recent reports, here is the agent with no tracing. Each tool section adds one tracing file that imports these files and changes nothing in them.

run-plain.ts runs all three questions:.

LangSmith traces the plain openai package with two helpers. wrapOpenAI records each model call, and traceable records your own functions. Without traceable on the run and the tools, wrapOpenAI alone gave three separate root runs and no tool runs.

This file adds 25 lines and removes 3, and installs one package.

LangSmith showed one root run with five children in call order: LLM, get_order_status, LLM, get_refund_policy, LLM. Every field it recorded became a row of the checklist table under "Results". Cost appeared only after a custom price entry. In our error run the failing tool was marked as an error, but the root stayed success: traceable turned the throw into a rejected promise that our agent did not await, so the agent carried on and answered.

Langfuse self-hosts as six containers, including ClickHouse, a column store built for large scans. In our measurement the stack held 2.60–2.64 GiB of memory at idle. Its Docker Compose guide recommends at least 4 CPU cores and 16 GiB RAM, with about 100 GiB of disk.

Industry observers note that the TypeScript path is built on OpenTelemetry. You start the OTel Node SDK with LangfuseSpanProcessor, wrap the client with observeOpenAI, and wrap your own functions with observe:.

This file adds 31 lines and removes 5, and installs four packages. We pinned the OTel Node SDK to 0.223.0, because @langfuse/otel 6.1.1 does not accept 0.300.0.

In a recent development, langfuse successfully recreated the same trace tree, neatly tagging the spans as AGENT, GENERATION, and TOOL. It captured all the essentials: tool calls, tool definitions, and the complete message history. However, for the LLM output, it only saved the assistant's message—dropping the finish_reason, response ID, and the provider name.

We ran our deployment in Langfuse v4's events_only mode, which turns off the v1 trace endpoint. Because of this, the API didn't return a centralized trace object or root-level sums for tokens and costs, even though the UI calculated and displayed them perfectly (we didn't test other modes).

Costs highlighted up exactly as expected once we added a custom price entry. Since Langfuse calculates prices based on the specific usage types you define, and we only set rates for input and output, the separate reasoning tokens went unpriced. Finally, during our error test, the observe wrapper let the error bubble up to the agent, correctly flagging both the tool and the root span as an ERROR.

Recent findings suggest that phoenix self-hosts as two containers, one Python server and Postgres. In our measurement it held 0.47 GiB at idle. Phoenix is source-available under the Elastic License 2.0, so it is not open source. Authentication is off until you turn it on.

The TypeScript path uses Phoenix's register() helper and the OpenInference instrumentation for the OpenAI package. OpenInference is a set of OpenTelemetry attribute names for LLM spans. traceAgent and traceTool wrap the run and the tools:.

This file adds 32 lines and removes 3, and installs three packages.

Phoenix rebuilt the same tree, typed as AGENT, LLM and TOOL. Each LLM span keeps the full OpenAI response object, plus the messages as flattened attributes. The root span stores no token count, but Phoenix computes a sum for the root and the trace when you read it. Cost and those sums are only in the GraphQL API and the UI, and the REST API has no per-trace endpoint.

Cost appeared after a custom price entry under Settings > Models, and Phoenix priced the reasoning tokens by falling back to the output price. In the error run, the tool span and the root were marked ERROR, and the tool span carried an exception event with the stack trace.

Opik self-hosts as eight containers, including ClickHouse, MySQL and ZooKeeper. In our measurement it held 3.69 GiB at idle, the most of the four. The self-hosted UI opened without a login, so every trace was readable from any machine that could reach the port.

It has been revealed that the TypeScript path wraps the client with trackOpenAI and your own functions with track. By default trackOpenAI starts a new trace for every model call, so the file passes the run's span through the documented parent option:.

According to recent reports, this file adds 33 lines and removes 5. It installs opik-openai 2.2.142, and npm adds opik 1.11.14 as its peer, because opik-openai asks for opik ^1.8.61.

Opik successfully recreated the trace tree, and its trace object neatly tallies token counts across all LLM spans. In the logs, tool arguments are bundled into an array, and the LLM output only retains the assistant's message.

Recent findings suggest that we did notice a quirk with the documented OpenAI wrapper (tested on the npm package opik 1.11.14): it tags model calls as general rather than llm, which incorrectly leaves the llm_span_count at zero. (We didn't test newer Opik core versions to see if this has changed). Additionally, because our synchronous tools execute in under a millisecond, they log the exact same start time as the subsequent LLM call, causing the UI to list the LLM call first out of order.

Cost tracking is entirely manual. Opik showed no costs by default, and the documentation doesn't mention a custom price table. We checked the configuration tabs on our 2.2.52 instance (Feedback definitions, AI Providers, Workspace preferences) and found no model pricing settings. To see costs, you have to manually assign a price to each individual span yourself—only the spans we hardcoded this way displayed a cost.

Sources indicate that finally, error reporting is highly detailed. If something fails, Opik attaches an error_info block—complete with the error type, message, and full traceback—directly to the tool span, the root span, and the overall trace.

Sources indicate that acruxCore self-hosts as five containers: Postgres, Redis, a Node API and worker, and nginx. In our measurement it held 0.39 GiB at idle, the least of the four. Its quickstart leaves sign-up open and ships a committed default GATEWAY_ENCRYPTION_KEY, which encrypts stored provider keys; replace it. We tested a local build from 2026-09-17.

Industry observers note that the TypeScript path AcruxCore's docs put first is its gateway. The official openai client keeps working: you point its baseURL at ACRUXCORE_BASE_URL + "/gateway" and call a model registered in AcruxCore, which forwards each call to an OpenAI-compatible provider. The gateway records every model call as an llm span. The SDK's step helpers add the rest: traces.step opens the agent span, traces.wrap wraps each tool, and two headers file the gateway's spans under the agent span:.

In a recent development, this file adds 30 lines and removes 5, and installs one package. It builds its own client, so it does not use provider.ts. The gateway refused our team API key, so the client uses a gateway virtual key created in the dashboard.

In a recent development, on this path every model call passes through the AcruxCore server, which none of the other four tools need. If you do not want a proxy in the request path, the SDK's register() helper sends OpenTelemetry spans from your process instead. On that path the step helpers do not join the openai package's spans, so you write the agent and tool spans by hand.

AcruxCore rebuilt the same tree, typed as agent, llm and tool, in call order. Each LLM span keeps the full response, the provider and the cached-token count, and the trace carries a token total. The LLM spans do not keep the tool definitions sent to the model, and no reasoning-token count was recorded. The trace took its name from the question, not from the agent span, and each LLM span is named by its start time.

According to recent reports, cost appeared on every LLM span and as a sum on the trace, from the custom price we set on the model in AcruxCore's model list. In the error run, the step helpers marked the tool span and the agent root as error with the error message, with no status code of ours. The API returned no stack trace.

All five tools accept traces over OTLP, the OpenTelemetry wire format. trace-otel.ts sends the same spans with no vendor package: the OTel Node SDK, the OTLP/HTTP protobuf exporter and the OpenInference OpenAI instrumentation. The exporter reads its endpoint and headers from environment variables:.

We ran the two-tool question once per backend and changed only environment variables: the endpoint, the headers, and for Phoenix a resource attribute that sets the project name (without it, spans go to a default project). "Accepted" means the exporter reported success, which it does only for an HTTP 2xx, and we read the spans back through each API.

Opik stored the root and tool spans as general although AGENT and TOOL kinds were sent; the cause is Not tested. LangSmith mapped AGENT to its chain type. If you instrument with plain OTel and OpenInference attributes, your raw spans are not tied to one vendor, but span types, cost and trace views still differ by backend.

The first table covers setup: how much server each tool needs, how much code we changed in the agent, and how cost and the plain OTel exporter worked. Phoenix and AcruxCore had the smallest servers, and AcruxCore needed the fewest lines among the self-hosted tools. Opik was the only one without a price table.

Industry observers note that the second table checks each trace against what LangSmith recorded for the same run, one field at a time. All five rebuilt the same tree with tokens and durations. They differ in span types, how much of the LLM output they keep, where token sums live, and how much detail they store for the failing tool.

In a recent development, token totals for the two-tool question ranged from 1,910 to 2,111. Each tool traced a separate run and reasoning length varies, so these numbers do not compare the tools.

All five tools successfully traced our test agent, so the right choice really comes down to your team's specific constraints, infrastructure preferences, and how tracing fits into the rest of your MLOps tooling.

Recent findings suggest that all four alternatives successfully recreated LangSmith’s trace tree. The real deciding factors are boilerplate code, span typing, cost tracking, and server bloat.

In a recent development, langSmith remains the simplest option for LangChain users who can utilize the cloud. Otherwise, your choice depends on your priorities: Langfuse for community size, Phoenix for a lightweight Postgres footprint, Opik for strict Apache-2.0 compliance with deep error logging, or AcruxCore for combined tracing and tool governance on minimal hardware. Best of all, if you stick to standard OpenTelemetry spans, you aren't locked in—you can try them all and easily pivot later.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A one-of-a-kind SpongeBob SquarePants trading card featuring Squidward’s “Bold and Brash” self-portrait sold for $58,560 at Goldin’s November 14 auction.

The card comes from Topps’ 2025 SpongeBob SquarePants 25th Anniversary set, its first SpongeBob release since 2009. Topps made 25 copies of the standard “Bold and Brash” card and just one gold-foil version, known as a Superfractor. That’s the copy that went up for auction.

The artwork comes from “Artist Unknown,” half of a 2001 Season 2 episode that aired alongside “Sailor Mouth.”.

A true masterpiece 🖼️From 2025 Topps Chrome SpongeBob, this 1-of-1 Superfractor of Squidward’s “Bold and Brash” self-portrait just sold for $58,560. pic.twitter.com/uBaMOxS3SS.

In a recent development, PSA shared the sale price on November 17 alongside a photo of the card in its Topps-sealed case. The result came within $3,050 of the $61,610 Goldin previously took in for a PSA 10 card from the same set featuring SpongeBob himself. That red-foil card was one of five copies.

Sources indicate that in “Artist Unknown,” Squidward teaches a community art class and gets SpongeBob as his only student. When art collector Monty P. Moneybags drops in looking for pieces for his museum, Squidward indicates him “Bold and Brash,” an abstract self-portrait with his long nose and drooping limbs set against a bright yellow background.

“More like ‘Belongs in the Trash,’” Moneybags replies. A janitor then tosses the painting into his garbage can while Squidward watches.

A subreddit dedicated to the meme appeared in 2013, with fans posting edits that swapped in characters like Sonic the Hedgehog. Others made their own replicas, including one that ended up in the collection of Squidward voice actor Rodger Bumpass.

In a recent development, the joke has since made its way onto real wall art. Hot Topic has sold both wood and canvas versions of the portrait that Bikini Bottom’s art collector sent to the trash.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Content creator Catalina Fernández, known online as Cata Amatista, has died at the age of 25 after a years-long battle with brain cancer, her family confirmed.

The influencer had amassed more than 3 million followers across Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, where she documented her cancer diagnosis, treatments, and daily life while living with the disease.

Fernández first revealed her diagnosis in July 2023 and continued sharing updates about her health over the following three years. Her family announced her death in a statement posted to Instagram on November 12, 2026.

In a statement shared with her followers, Fernández’s family confirmed that she had died after living with a cancerous brain tumor.

It has been revealed that “Today, Cata has departed from this material plane,” her family wrote. “Her body has found rest, but her light, her love, and all the wonderful things she sowed in this world remain forever within each of us.”.

The family also reflected on her personality and the impact she had on those around her throughout her life.

“Cata was — and will always be — an extraordinary being of light. She was a child full of love, life, joy, and dreams, possessing a beautiful gift for finding magic in the smallest of things,” they continued.

“Until her very last moment, she taught us how to live, to be grateful, to enjoy life, to offer tight embraces, and to understand that life is a gift worth celebrating every single day.”.

A post shared by cata✿ (@cataamatista).

Fernández had been open about her health since July 2023, when she uploaded a YouTube video revealing that she had been diagnosed with cerebellar medulloblastoma, a type of cancerous brain tumor that develops in the cerebellum.

TikToker Andreethegirl shares heartbreaking final video with fans after her death.

Over the following years, she underwent multiple treatments, including surgery and chemotherapy, while regularly sharing updates from medical appointments and documenting her experiences for her audience.

Her content attracted millions of followers across social media, with viewers following her treatment journey alongside other aspects of her daily life.

In their announcement, her family emphasized that they wanted Fernández to be remembered for more than her illness.

According to recent reports, “If there is one thing we want you to take away from Cata, it is this: cancer was not her whole story. Her story was love — the way she chose to live, the joy with which she embraced each day, and the light she shared even when the path became difficult,” they wrote.

“We choose to remember her not through her absence, but through everything she gave us; for there are some people who do not need to remain physically present to stay with us forever.”.

Following the announcement, fans flooded the comments of her social media posts with condolences and messages remembering the creator.

“Rest in peace, you were a warrior in every way, we will always remember you,” one follower commented.

According to recent reports, “You fought so hard! Your leaving hurts,” another wrote.

It has been revealed that A third added: “Rest in peace my beautiful Cata. You were too strong.”.

Industry observers note that customer reviews are often displayed on business websites, but presenting them effectively requires more than adding a few star icons and customer quotes. Developers need to consider semantic HTML, responsive layouts, accessibility, and how review content fits into the overall user experience.

According to recent reports, A well-built review section makes customer feedback easy to read without distracting visitors from the rest of the page. It should also work across different screen sizes and remain understandable to people using assistive technologies.

Let's look at how to build one using standard HTML and CSS.

Industry observers note that the first step is to structure review content properly. Instead of placing everything inside generic elements, use meaningful HTML elements to describe the content.

For example, a review can use as its container and for the customer's actual feedback.

Industry observers note that this structure separates the review from its attribution and gives the section a clear heading. The rating also includes an accessible label so screen-reader customers can understand what the stars represent.

For real websites, developers should display genuine customer feedback and avoid presenting invented testimonials as actual customer experiences.

Industry observers note that A review section might look attractive on a desktop but become difficult to read on smaller screens. CSS Grid provides a straightforward way to create a flexible layout without relying on JavaScript.

The auto-fit and minmax() combination allows cards to adjust to the available space. Instead of defining a fixed number of columns for every device, the browser fits as many cards as the container can comfortably accommodate.

Developers working with more complex interfaces can explore SitePoint's guide to responsive web design for additional layout techniques.

A responsive layout should remain readable when viewed on a phone. Avoid fixed card widths, excessive padding, and text sizes that force users to zoom.

You can also adjust spacing at smaller viewport widths:.

Test the section at several viewport sizes rather than relying on one desktop preview. Check that long customer names wrap correctly, cards do not overflow, and text remains comfortable to read.

Some review components use animated sliders, automatic scrolling, or hover effects. These features can create problems for visitors who prefer reduced motion or navigate with a keyboard.

Recent findings suggest that A simple approach is to avoid unnecessary animation. If transitions are included, respect the visitor's system preference:.

The MDN guide to using media queries for accessibility explains how developers can adapt interfaces to user preferences.

Also make sure interactive controls have visible keyboard focus styles. A carousel should provide usable previous and next controls, clear labels, and a way to pause automatic movement if it is used.

In a recent development, on a production website, reviews may come from a database, a content management system, or an external review service. Keeping the content separate from the presentation makes the component easier to maintain.

Businesses can also use an online reputation management platform to monitor customer feedback and understand how their brand is perceived across online channels.

For example, a developer could store each review with fields such as:.

In a recent development, the frontend can then render the same component for every review. This avoids manually creating separate HTML for each customer and makes future design changes easier.

Developers should also validate incoming data, handle missing fields, and avoid displaying private customer information without permission.

Before publishing, check the component in different browsers and screen sizes. Test keyboard navigation, screen-reader labels, text wrapping, and color contrast. If reviews are loaded dynamically, check how the section behaves when there are no reviews or when the data request fails.

A useful review component does not need complicated animations or a large JavaScript library. Semantic HTML, flexible CSS Grid layouts, accessible labels, and reliable content handling provide a strong foundation.

Customer feedback can only be useful on a website when visitors can understand and navigate it easily. By treating reviews as a proper interface component rather than decorative content, developers can create sections that are maintainable, accessible, and consistent with the rest of the website.

Meanwhile, a separate account called @kurwashibamaste had been feeding Centro Leaks rumors about the games since July. It claimed a development build appeared to lack fresh evolutions for Eevee and Tropius. It also claimed voice acting had been planned but had disappeared from recent builds.

On November 17, an X user posted a screenshot appearing to show Moot and @kurwashibamaste in the same account switcher. Moot responded with a GIF captioned “How it feels to spread misinformation and lies.” Centro then remarked Moot had admitted to running the alternate account and faking many of its Winds & Waves rumors.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A free Christian parody of Grand Theft Auto is launching alongside GTA 6, and getting five stars will bring Satan after you instead of the cops.

In a recent development, with players finally jumping into Vice City, satire site The Babylon Bee is opening up a city of its own. The game is called Grand Faith Auto, and it takes place in Upcoming Mercy, a 3D open world you can explore right in your browser.

The setup will look familiar to anyone who’s played GTA, as there are cars to take, storefronts and billboards dotted around the city, and a radar to help you find your way.

But while the real thing often throws you into the criminal underworld, Grand Faith Auto is all about being an upstanding citizen.

Recent findings suggest that instead of the traditional Wanted level, doing good deeds earns you stars of divine approval. Get all five, and the devil himself comes looking for you instead of the cops.

One of the deeds you can do around Upcoming Mercy is pull a driver out of their car and preach to them before driving off in it yourself. You can also offer a “Lady of the Night” a lift to church, or try to feed the hungry in a scenario involving a closed chicken restaurant, a deli under attack, and a box of pocket Bibles.

There’s even a stealth mission where you sneak into a cartel warehouse and swap its drugs for little figurines. You’ll have to stay out of sight, because getting spotted by a guard is an instant fail.

The official Grand Faith Auto game launch trailer. It's the new hit video game everyone's been waiting to play for years. Available November 18!Grand Faith Auto is free, while Grand Theft Auto VI will cost your eternal soul (plus $80).Just go to https://t.co/21fFFTXowv pic.twitter.com/aBJRRtTeZY.

Recent findings suggest that you’re not completely unarmed, though, as you can wield a holy shotgun to fend off the imps tracking you down. A shot to the head stuns them, leaving you free to kick them back to hell. After that, the instructions tell you to go to church.

Police can’t wait for GTA 6 to be released so they can “catch a break”.

GTA 6 forces you to take your time with the main story instead of speedrunning it.

GTA 6 best guides for launch: Everything you need to know.

Discussing the game in an X post, The Baylon Bee CEO Seth Dillon remarked that he doesn’t expect the game to actually rival GTA 6, it’s just a “Christian alternative.”.

That’s probably for the best, given that GTA 6 has already become the joint-best-reviewed game of all time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hershey’s is bringing back its original five-cent chocolate bar price for one day only to celebrate the theatrical release of its new movie, giving customers several ways to take advantage of the promotion.

The chocolate organization is celebrating the November 25 debut of Hershey, a biographical film exploring the lives of Milton Hershey and his wife, Catherine “Kitty” Hershey, with a limited-time deal inspired by the brand’s history.

The promotion will allow customers to purchase classic Hershey’s Milk Chocolate Bars for just a nickel, matching their original price from 1900. However, the process for claiming the discount varies depending on where customers shop.

The promotion will take place on Wednesday, November 25, with discounted chocolate bars available through Hershey’s Chocolate World, Walmart, and Amazon Grocery.

Customers visiting Hershey’s Chocolate World locations in Hershey, Pennsylvania, or Times Square in Latest York City can purchase the bars for five cents each beginning at 9 AM local time.

Recent findings suggest that there is a limit of 10 bars per person, and the offer cannot be combined with other discounts. Applicable taxes will still be charged.

In a recent development, walmart customers can also take advantage of the promotion through two different methods. Those shopping online can purchase a classic Hershey’s Milk Chocolate Bar for five cents by placing an online pickup order through Walmart.com using their Walmart account.

Meanwhile, customers shopping at Walmart stores can receive the discounted price through the Ibotta app. After purchasing a qualifying chocolate bar, shoppers must upload a photo of their receipt to receive cash back.

Walmart’s promotion is limited to five bars per person and does not apply to orders shipped directly to customers’ homes.

7 Brew adds food to its menu for the first time with five new $3 treats.

Reese’s adds bizarre warning to Halloween candy after $5 million lawsuit.

Amazon Grocery will also participate in the promotion, offering five-cent chocolate bars through same-day delivery in select markets.

In a recent development, customers with qualifying delivery addresses can use a promotional code shared through Hershey’s social media channels to receive free shipping at checkout. The offer is limited to two bars per customer while supplies last, with taxes calculated based on the total order.

“The five-cent bar gives fans a chance to experience a sweet piece of Hershey’s story for themselves,” the tech giant said in a statement shared with PEOPLE.

“Bringing it back on the day HERSHEY debuts in theaters gives fans a fun way to celebrate the brand’s roots and the story that inspired it.”.

Alongside the promotion, Hershey’s is introducing vintage-inspired packaging for several products, including its Milk Chocolate Bars and Kisses chocolates.

The packaging features the organization’s historic wordmark, Milton Hershey’s signature, and typography inspired by the brand’s early years. Each package also includes a QR code directing customers to more information about Hershey’s history.

The upcoming movie stars Finn Wittrock as Milton Hershey and Alexandra Daddario as Catherine Hershey, following their relationship and the development of the chocolate manufacturer.

Directed by Mark Waters and filmed in Pennsylvania, the movie also features Alan Ruck, David Costabile, Richard Kind, and several other cast members.

1. Define the question before collecting data Consider a hypothetical development board that disconnects when a peripheral starts. Several explanations remain possible: a firmware exception, a transport problem, or a power supply concern. Start with a testable question: “Does the measured supply voltage change when this peripheral starts?” That question tells you what to record and what to keep constant.

Rockstar has cut longtime ways to hook up with other characters in GTA 6, including hiring sex workers, as it builds the game’s romance around Jason and Lucia.

According to recent reports, GTA 3 let players pay for sex back in 2001, and later games gave them more ways to pursue other characters. San Andreas gave CJ six potential girlfriends, while GTA 4 let Niko Bellic meet dates through the in-game internet.

GTA 5 kept paid hookups and gave players another option at the Vanilla Unicorn strip club. Flirting with certain dancers during a private dance could lead to leaving the club with them, hooking up, and calling them again later.

GTA 6 still puts Jason in suggestive situations in the main story with side characters attempting to seduce him, and strangers around Leonida flirt with him openly and invite him into explicit situations. But unlike GTA games from before, that’s as intimate as Jason is allowed to get.

Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier remarked a trip to the strip club was the closest he found to a way to cheat on Lucia, and he later confirmed you cannot kiss anyone except your partner.

You can't kiss anyone except your partner.

The Guardian’s review confirmed that either lead can get a private dance on their own or the couple can go together. Shacknews confirmed that players can no longer pick up sex workers.

Industry observers note that rockstar described Jason and Lucia as “a couple in a bind, lovers on the run” in a statement to Shacknews. The studio mentioned it chose which features to bring forward based on how they fit the story and the gameplay systems it wanted to expand.

GTA 6 is giving players more freedom to complete missions their own way.

GTA 6 almost had four playable characters instead of just Jason and Lucia.

GTA 6 confirms realistic NPCs, deeper relationships, body changes, social media system & more.

“While we have taken a lot forward from previous GTA titles, everything we have implemented in VI has been done to support the spirit of the story… Many aspects of previous titles are not present in GTAVI, but the elements we have we believe are all necessary and complementary to the feeling and motivations we wanted to emphasize as you play through Jason and Lucia’s story.”.

Industry observers note that GTA 6 gives players several ways to build intimacy between the two leads. Jason and Lucia can go dancing, hold hands, and make each other coffee. The couple can also become more affectionate and intimate when the relationship is going well.

In a recent development, how romantic that partnership becomes is up to the player. Rockstar development head Rob Nelson has said players can let the romance cool while Jason and Lucia continue to work together as the story unfolds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An Arizona judge ordered YouTuber Lane Myers released from prison after county prosecutors raised doubts about an email that helped send him there.

Myers, 43, pleaded guilty in July 2025 to felony stalking and harassment charges involving Shannon Walker, the wife of Tucson city prosecutor Matthew Walker. He was placed on probation under conditions that restricted what he could post about the couple.

According to recent reports, in October 2026, Pima County Superior Court Judge Douglas Metcalf sentenced Myers to three years in prison for violating that probation. Prosecutors stated Myers had posted upcoming YouTube videos about the Walkers and argued those videos prompted others to send Shannon Walker threatening and harassing emails.

Investigators tied at least one of those emails to an IP address associated with the Walkers’ home, casting doubt on whether the message came from someone reacting to Myers’ videos. Who sent it remains under investigation.

Deputy County Attorney Rachel Stiles submitted the upcoming evidence under seal and discussed it only in broad terms at the November 17 hearing.

Tucson police searched the Walkers’ home on November 2 and seized several devices, including Matthew Walker’s city-issued laptop. County prosecutors first asked for Myers’ release at an emergency hearing the next day. On November 5, the city of Tucson put Matthew Walker on paid administrative leave while police investigated possible misconduct connected to the probation case.

A Tucson YouTuber was ordered freed from prison after county prosecutors found evidence suggesting the victim or her husband, a city prosecutor, may have drafted harassing emails that helped put him behind bars. https://t.co/An6DVVsuFD.

Recent findings suggest that metcalf returned Myers to probation on November 17, and his 2025 stalking and harassment convictions still stand. Myers thanked county prosecutors in a statement for bringing the evidence forward, and thanked Metcalf for “giving me the opportunity to show I can follow conditions.”.

Stiles said county prosecutors still believe Myers violated his probation and will review the evidence before deciding whether to ask the court to revoke it again. Metcalf scheduled a status hearing for December 8.

GQ’s reviewer also came across a fursuited character under a helicopter spotlight and saw armed police take them down.

Korean gaming outlet Inven shared footage of the roadside standoff. Kinda Funny’s Andy Cortez had described a similar encounter back in August, when he heard a helicopter warn that a furry was on the loose during a private preview at Rockstar North.

The clips and screenshots have drawn mixed reactions. Burger King is bringing a massive burger inspired by the Grand Theft Auto franchise into the real world, introducing a seven-patty Whopper based on a fictional fast-food restaurant featured in the games.

The upcoming creation, called the HeartWhopper, is part of a limited-time promotion from Burger King Belgium that allows GTA fans to win a real version of the oversized burger.

The campaign debuts on November 19 and takes inspiration from the fictional fast-food chain found throughout the GTA series, turning one of its recognizable menu items into an actual meal.

The HeartWhopper features seven flame-grilled beef patties stacked with cheese, tomato slices, lettuce, and onion rings, recreating the exaggerated burgers associated with the fictional restaurant.

According to Burger King, the promotion is intended as a parody of the video game franchise’s own parody of fast-food chains, with the company claiming its restaurants have served as inspiration for fictional businesses in gaming.

Rather than introducing the HeartWhopper as a traditional menu item, Burger King Belgium is giving players the chance to win one through a social media competition.

A post shared by Burger King BE & LUX (@burgerkingbe).

To participate, fans must share a video clip showing themselves enjoying a burger from the in-game restaurant and tag either Burger King Belgium or Burger King Luxembourg.

The company will select the most creative submission each day, awarding the winner a real-life HeartWhopper. The competition will run for two weeks, giving players multiple opportunities to participate.

Burger King is also promoting the campaign through YouTube advertisements, YouTube Shorts, and gaming communities on Reddit, with teasers released ahead of the November 19 launch.

Breaking: Prompt Management in TypeScript: LangSmith vs Git vs 3 Open-Source Registries

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1718 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sitepoint

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.
  • Sources indicate that 7 Day Free Trial.
  • Every prompt registry we tested can change a prompt in a running TypeScript app, roll it back, and give production and staging different versions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Weekly. Free. One click to leave.

Sources indicate that 7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

Every prompt registry we tested can change a prompt in a running TypeScript app, roll it back, and give production and staging different versions. LangSmith's prompt hub, Langfuse, Phoenix and AcruxCore all passed those three tests. The real differences show up elsewhere: which template syntax each one accepts, how many npm packages it pulls in, how long a change takes to reach the app, and what happens when the registry is down.

We tested all of this with one small app and one prompt, which has a condition and a loop. Git files served as the baseline. Every number below comes from a recorded run.

In a recent development, most teams start with prompts in code: a template string, or a .txt file next to the code that uses it. That works until a product manager wants to change one sentence, and the change has to wait for a full release.

It has been revealed that A prompt registry moves the text out of the deploy. The app fetches the prompt by name and by a label such as production. You change which version the label points to, and the app picks up the fresh text without a deploy.

LangSmith's prompt hub is the best-known registry, but it is not the only one. Several of the LangSmith alternatives also manage prompts, and three of them are open source and self-hostable: Langfuse, Phoenix and AcruxCore. We covered how those tools handle tracing in Self-Hosted LangSmith Alternatives: 4 Tools Tested on One TypeScript Agent. This article covers prompts only.

Every tool got the same prompt, support-reply. Its template takes three variables: a customer name, a plan, and a list of help articles. It has one condition: a priority line appears only for premium customers. It also has one loop: one line per help article. In Jinja2 syntax, the template looks like this:.

One help article contains the text Settings > Export. We included it on purpose, to catch any tool that HTML-escapes > into >.

Every tool then ran the same sequence from a TypeScript script:.

Each tool used its own documented TypeScript SDK. The four registries passed all six steps. The rest of this article covers how each one got there, and what it cost.

Recent findings suggest that keeping prompts in the repository costs almost nothing. The template sits in prompts/support-reply.njk, and nunjucks, the JavaScript port of Jinja2, renders it:.

According to recent reports, the autoescape: false line matters. Our first version called nunjucks.renderString() directly, and the test failed. The default environment HTML-escapes its output, so Settings > Export reached the model as Settings > Export. Escaping is correct for web pages and wrong for prompts.

In a recent development, git gives you full Jinja2, code review on every prompt change, and history in the same place as the code. What it can't do is change a prompt in a running app. Every edit, and every rollback, waits for a deploy.

According to recent reports, langSmith stores a prompt as a serialized LangChain object (ChatPromptTemplate), not as plain text. LangSmith's own documentation says you must use the LangChain npm package to pull prompts in TypeScript (Manage prompts programmatically). So a plain TypeScript app that uses the openai package still needs langchain and @langchain/core:.

Industry observers note that those three packages installed 23 packages and 70 MB. Most of the size is @langchain/* (27 MB) and js-tiktoken (22 MB).

In a recent development, templates. In TypeScript, LangChain accepts f-string and mustache templates. Mustache sections ({{#docs}}…{{/docs}}) handled our loop. Mustache has no ==, though, so the premium check became an is_premium boolean computed in code. We also tried templateFormat: "jinja2", which LangChain's Python package supports. In TypeScript it threw DEFAULT_PARSER_MAPPING[templateFormat] is not a function.

Sources indicate that labels and rollback. production and staging are reserved tags, and the documentation moves them in the UI. The langsmith JavaScript client has no public method that moves a tag. Our script called the same REST route the SDK uses internally (POST /api/v1/repos/-//tags). It worked, but it is not a documented API.

Caching. The SDK caches prompts for 300 seconds by default. In our test, a running app saw the upcoming version 300 seconds after we moved the tag.

Langfuse's TypeScript client is one package, @langfuse/client. It installed 5 packages and 8 MB:.

Creating a version, moving a label and reading by label are all public SDK calls: prompt.create, prompt.revision and prompt.get (Get started with prompt management).

Templates. The documentation indicates only {{variable}} substitution. But compile() calls the mustache library, so sections worked for our loop. The type signature accepts only string values, so passing a list needed a cast. The Langfuse UI colours the section tags red, and it lists title and body as the prompt's variables, not docs or is_premium. We would not depend on behaviour the documentation doesn't promise. When we sent the Jinja2 version instead, Langfuse returned the {% if %} and {% for %} tags unchanged, with no error. The model would have received them as text.

Sources indicate that caching. The cache time is 60 seconds by default (Caching). Our app saw the change after 62 seconds. Langfuse is also the only client with a fallback option: a prompt string the SDK uses when it cannot reach the server on a cold start.

According to recent reports, phoenix's TypeScript client fetches a prompt by name and tag, and toSDK() converts it into the message format the openai package expects. Phoenix templates only replace variables, so the condition and the loop have to run in your code before rendering:.

That is 16 lines, against 6 to 8 for the other registries. All the extra lines are template logic that now lives in the app.

Templates. Phoenix offers MUSTACHE, F_STRING and NONE formats (Prompts reference). Even in MUSTACHE mode, though, rendering is a plain replacement of {{name}}. When we sent mustache sections, they came back unchanged, with no error.

Errors. getPrompt() catches every error, logs it and returns null. You can see this in the client source, src/utils/getPromptBySelector.ts. A missing prompt and an unreachable server look the same to your code, which is why the snippet checks for null.

It has been revealed that size and caching. The client installed 57 packages and 90 MB. Most of that is OpenTelemetry, which comes in through its @arizeai/phoenix-otel dependency. The client has no prompt cache, so every render is a network call. That is also why a label change showed up immediately: 0 seconds in our test.

Sources indicate that acruxCore stores Jinja2 templates and renders them on the server with nunjucks. The SDK sends the variables and gets back finished messages:.

The template from the test section works as it is, condition and loop included, with no is_premium flag computed in code. A label is called an alias here, and promoteAlias() moves it (Manage prompts via the SDK). The SDK installed 3 packages and 12 MB. Most of the 12 MB is one OpenTelemetry package, @opentelemetry/semantic-conventions.

Sources indicate that templates. Jinja2 only. When we committed the mustache version, AcruxCore rejected it at commit time with Template parse error: unexpected token: #. That is a clear error, but it also means that moving mustache prompts from LangSmith or Langfuse requires rewriting them.

We sent the same two templates, a Jinja2 one and a mustache one, to each tool's own renderer:.

It has been revealed that the rows that matter most are the ones where the tags were left in the output, because those failures produce no error. The model receives raw template syntax, and the only symptom is a strange answer. Whatever tool you pick, test one prompt with logic in it before you move the rest.

It has been revealed that putting logic in the template is not automatically better. It lets someone change the condition without a deploy. It also lets them break the condition without a deploy. Keeping logic in code, as Phoenix forces you to do, puts every branch under code review and in your tests.

A registry is a new runtime dependency, so we tested an outage. The app reached each registry through a local proxy, and we switched the proxy off. A separate process then started while the registry was still unreachable.

It has been revealed that langSmith, Langfuse and AcruxCore keep serving the last good version while the registry is down, even after the cache time has passed. The risk is a cold start: a latest container or a serverless function that boots during the outage. Langfuse's fallback option is the built-in answer to that. With the other tools, keep a copy of each prompt in your code as a fallback, which brings back part of the Git setup.

Recent findings suggest that keep prompts in Git if engineers make every prompt change and your deploys are quick. Set autoescape: false, and you get Jinja2, reviews and history for free.

Use LangSmith's prompt hub if you already use LangChain, or already trace with LangSmith. If your app doesn't use LangChain, budget for the extra dependency and for the tag moves that only the UI supports.

Industry observers note that use Langfuse if you want a small client, a local compile(), and a fallback for cold starts. Keep to {{variable}} substitution unless you are comfortable relying on mustache behaviour that the documentation doesn't promise.

It has been revealed that use Phoenix if you already use it for tracing, or if you prefer all template logic in code. Remember the null check, and that every render is a network call.

According to recent reports, use AcruxCore if you want real conditions and loops in the template and rendering on the server. Expect one network call per newly introduced set of variables, and a personal API key for writes.

In a recent development, before you choose, run one of your own prompts with real logic in it through the tool's SDK, not through its playground. Two of the four registries we tested failed on template syntax without any error, and an SDK run is where you would see that.

GTA 6 players in Japan have voiced disappointment over the game’s censored content, which tones down nudity and gore compared with the Western release.

Japan is no stranger when it comes to censoring video games, with recent examples like Resident Evil Requiem famously featuring black textures over decapitated body parts and less blood.

However, on November 10, it was revealed that the Japanese version of GTA 6 was 1 GB smaller than its overseas brother. This swiftly sparked fears among players that the game would be missing content to make it pass Japan’s ratings board. Well, it turns out that those fears were indeed true.

In a recent development, A screenshot of protagonist Jason taking a shower in the Japanese version of the game has gone viral, and no, it’s not because he’s getting all soapy. Rather, it’s because he’s showering in what can only be described as a tiny black Speedo.

For contrast, the overseas release has Jason showering in his birthday suit, with there being no steam or swimwear to obstruct his bare buttocks from view. As you can imagine, many fans aren’t exactly happy with these watered-down scenes.

“Isn’t it strange that in a country where people go completely naked in public baths and hot springs, they make people wear swimsuits to take a shower?” wrote one Japanese player.

Recent findings suggest that “If they’re going out of their way to give it a CERO Z rating for 18+, what’s the point of censoring the content? I don’t get it,” replied another commenter.

Nudity isn’t the only thing that has been toned down, as Japanese gaming website Game*Spark found that the Japanese version has no option to adjust the intensity of blood and gore.

The Japanese version also has less blood left on the ground after gunfights, although dismemberment remains in the Japanese release.

“They could just use parental controls and the like to restrict content that’s harmful to children, but instead, decent adults get content shoved at them that’s been watered down to the point of having its teeth pulled,” added another angry fan.

GTA 6 was released on November 19 and is now the joint best-reviewed game of all time, sitting alongside The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

According to recent reports, AI-generated videos are becoming an important part of modern web design. Designers can now create animated backgrounds, product demonstrations, hero section videos, and visual storytelling elements without relying entirely on traditional video production. However, generating a visually appealing video is only one part of the process. To use AI-generated videos effectively on a website, developers and designers must also understand video formats, visual quality, file optimization, and website performance.

These technical factors directly influence how videos appear across devices, how rapidly pages load, and how smoothly visitors interact with a website.

Video format selection is one of the first technical decisions when preparing AI-generated assets for the web. Different formats offer different levels of compression, compatibility, and visual quality.

The most commonly used formats include:.

For most websites, MP4 with H.264 remains a dependable default. WebM or AV1 can be offered as additional formats where appropriate.

In a recent development, developers should also consider browser compatibility before selecting a format. Providing multiple sources allows browsers to choose a supported option.

Industry observers note that AI-generated videos can sometimes contain visual inconsistencies, unnatural movements, distorted objects, or changes in lighting between frames. These concerns become more noticeable when videos are displayed in large website sections.

In a recent development, resolution is an important factor in maintaining visual quality. Common resolutions include:.

Sources indicate that however, higher resolution does not automatically mean better website performance or user experience. A 4K video may look impressive, but loading it unnecessarily can increase bandwidth consumption.

According to recent reports, frame rate also affects the viewing experience. Many website videos work well at 24 or 30 frames per second. Higher frame rates may be useful for fast-moving scenes, but they also increase the amount of visual data that needs to be processed.

Designers should review AI-generated footage before publishing it. Checking transitions, motion consistency, sharpness, and color accuracy helps prevent distracting visual problems.

Large video files can significantly increase website loading times. This is especially important for websites with video backgrounds, animated landing pages, and multiple visual sections.

Video optimization involves reducing file size without making the footage noticeably worse.

Some practical optimization techniques include:.

Compression: Video compression reduces unnecessary data while preserving important visual details. Developers can use encoding tools such as FFmpeg to adjust bitrate, resolution, and codec settings.

It has been revealed that bitrate control: Bitrate determines how much data is used to represent each second of video. A higher bitrate generally preserves more detail but increases file size. Selecting an appropriate bitrate depends on the video's resolution, movement, and intended display size.

Trimming unnecessary footage: Website videos rarely need to be several minutes long. Removing unused sections helps reduce file size and keeps visual content focused.

Recent findings suggest that removing unnecessary audio: Background videos that do not require sound should be exported without an audio track. This reduces unnecessary data and supports a cleaner user experience.

According to recent reports, responsive video delivery: Websites should serve appropriately sized assets for different screen sizes. A smaller video may be sufficient for mobile consumers, while desktop visitors can receive a higher-resolution version.

These techniques help developers balance visual quality with efficient content delivery.

Even a well-optimized video can affect website performance if it is implemented incorrectly. Developers should consider how videos are loaded, displayed, and processed by browsers.

In a recent development, for example, automatically loading several large videos when a page opens can consume significant bandwidth. Instead, developers can use lazy loading strategies for videos that appear further down the page.

For background videos, the HTML video element offers several useful attributes:.

A simple implementation looks like this:.

It has been revealed that developers should also avoid autoplaying large videos unnecessarily. A static image can often provide a better experience on mobile devices or slower connections.

Performance testing tools such as Google Lighthouse and Chrome DevTools can help identify whether video assets are affecting loading speed, bandwidth usage, or rendering performance.

Technical optimization should not come at the expense of accessibility. Background videos should not distract consumers or make website content difficult to understand.

Developers should respect the prefers-reduced-motion media query, which allows users who prefer reduced animation to receive a less motion-intensive experience.

A suitable static background image can be displayed as an alternative.

Mobile compatibility is equally important. Smaller screens, limited data aims, and varying network conditions can make heavy video assets less practical. Testing videos on different devices and connection speeds helps identify potential problems before publication.

It has been revealed that AI-generated video assets offer exciting possibilities for modern web design, but their successful implementation requires more than creative output. Choosing suitable video formats, maintaining consistent visual quality, compressing files, and considering website performance are all essential parts of the development process.

By combining thoughtful video production with responsive delivery, accessibility considerations, and performance testing, designers and developers can create engaging websites without compromising loading speed or usability. As AI video technology continues to evolve, understanding these technical fundamentals will remain valuable for building efficient and visually appealing web experiences.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A high school in Pennsylvania has been forced to scrap a test of AI-powered metal detectors after regular student items were continually flagged as weapons.

Industry observers note that over the last few years, a number of places have updated their security systems, scrapping old metal detectors in favor of newer ones – you’ll have seen them at airports, for example. These up-to-date detectors are supposed to speed up the security process, but they can cause headaches.

That has been the case for the Hempfield Area High School in Pennsylvania, as they have been helping to test the new Wi-AI detection system from CurvePoint AI.

As per TechSpot, Wi-AI uses Wi-Fi signals to look for concealed weapons, with people having to walk near SensePods, which tracks movements without even using cameras.

However, according to WTAE-TV in Pittsburgh, everyday items that students need for school – including binders, water bottles, and batteries – have been routinely flagged as weapons.

“The detection is not what they were hoping to get from the technology side of things and so, we are in agreement that, moving forward, as far as going live, its just not a product that is ready for that activation,” Superintendent Dr. Mark Holtzman told the news outlet.

Skip Smith, the CEO of CurvePoint AI, noted that the school “served as a testing and evaluation site” rather than being a full “operational deployment.”.

Additionally, Holtzman noted that the system was “not near” the 95% accuracy rate that the system hoped to achieve.

According to recent reports, it isn’t the first time that similar systems have caused these sorts of headaches. Back in October 2025, a 16-year-old student in Baltimore was swarmed by armed police when an AI gun detection system falsely flagged a Doritos bag as a firearm. That system was shut down just a month later, too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Rockstar Games developer says he and his colleagues are worried about losing their jobs after GTA 6, despite the successful launch.

The long-awaited sequel arrived on November 19 to rave reviews, after racking up well over $1 billion in pre-orders, and is likely to be one of, if not the biggest, video game releases ever.

GTA 5 sold more than 230 million copies, and Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte notes the follow-up is expected to surpass it.

But for some of the people who made it, launch week also brings questions about what happens in the weeks and months that follow.

Uriarte, who works at Rockstar’s Edinburgh studio, raised those concerns in an opinion piece for The Guardian. He described the pressure game developers have come to expect on either side of a major launch.

“While the highs of a game release like this can be incredible, game workers have also come to expect other, less welcome side effects: intense overtime in the buildup and mass redundancies in the aftermath,” Uriarte wrote.

He pointed to job losses across the games industry to explain why those fears persist, even at Rockstar.

Recent findings suggest that “It states a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.”.

Sources indicate that as a result, Uriarte said he was voting in favor of union recognition because he wants staff to have a say in pay, bonuses, and working conditions. He said Rockstar has already introduced some overtime pay and wants to build on that so workers are paid for every hour they put in.

Rockstar Games could strike before GTA 6 launches over unionization.

GTA 6 devs demand no more ‘crunch’ from Rockstar over unionization.

Rockstar Games fires dozens of devs for “gross misconduct”.

He went on to admit that there has been no suggestion from Rockstar that layoffs are imminent, but that the fears are still there among staff.

“After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it’s hard not to worry about what the future holds,” he added.

Best AI Humanizer Tools Tested and Compared: 7 Options for Web Content

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.
  • The best AI humanizer for web content is the one that changes how a draft reads without changing what it notes.
  • To compare them on equal terms, we ran the same 103-word AI-written release note through each tool in November 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Sources indicate that weekly. Free. One click to leave.

7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

The best AI humanizer for web content is the one that changes how a draft reads without changing what it notes. If you need a specific tone, Humanize Max gives you four styles and three lengths in one run. If you already work in QuillBot or Grammarly, their humanizers fit the account you have. GPTinf, Humanize AI and Undetectable AI put an AI check next to the rewrite, and Ahrefs gives you quick variants of a short passage.

To compare them on equal terms, we ran the same 103-word AI-written release note through each tool in November 2026. It contains a product name, two image formats, a settings path and the word "must", so it demonstrates whether a tool keeps the details a reader acts on. We also checked every feature, limit and price on the vendor's own pages on the same day.

A humanizer earns its place only if its output needs fewer fixes than the draft you started with, and these six checks show whether a tool will do that for your content.

Recent findings suggest that humanize Max is a single-purpose humanizer: you paste an AI draft, upload a file or load the built-in sample, choose a style and a length, and get a rewritten version in a few seconds. The four styles are Academic, Casual, Creative and Formal, and the three lengths are Shorten, Standard and Expand, so you can turn a stiff feature description into casual blog copy and trim it in the same run.

Recent findings suggest that the result highlights every phrase it changed, which makes it quick to check whether a product name or a settings path came through. If the rewrite doesn't land, Run it again produces a different version of the whole text. At the time of writing, it takes up to 2,000 words per run and works without an account.

Pricing: Plans and limits are still being finalized, so check the site for current terms.

Best for: Rewriting AI drafts of blog posts, product pages and emails into a specific tone.

QuillBot's AI Humanizer sits next to its paraphraser, grammar checker and AI detector, which makes it a natural pick if you already use QuillBot for rewording. Basic mode is free for up to 125 words per run, while Advanced mode, which rewrites more deeply, comes with Premium (the pricing page also lists three Advanced uses on the free proposal). In our test, it asked us to create a free account before it indicated the first result.

Premium removes the word limit and adds Freeze words, which keeps the terms you choose unchanged, along with tone insights, a history of past runs and a Chrome extension that humanizes text inside ChatGPT and Gemini.

Industry observers note that pricing: Basic mode is free. Premium is listed at $8.33 a month, billed annually.

Best for: Quick fixes to a paragraph or two for writers who already use QuillBot.

In a recent development, GPTinf is a writing toolkit built around its humanizer, with an AI detector, plagiarism checker, grammar checker, paraphraser and readability checker on the same site. The humanizer has two modes, Standard and Academic, and takes pasted text or a PDF, Word or plain-text file. File-to-File mode returns the humanized document in its original format, so a long brief keeps its layout.

It has been revealed that custom Style lets you paste 150 to 1,200 words of your own writing, and later runs are shaped to match it, with no account needed. After each run, an AI-likelihood estimate appears under the output, so you can see whether a draft needs another pass. Treat that number as a probability, not proof of who wrote the text.

Pricing: A free plan is available. Paid plans start at $9.99 a month for Lite (5,000 words), with Pro at $24.99 and Unlimited at $59.99.

Best for: Freelancers and content teams that want to rewrite and check drafts without switching tools.

Grammarly's AI Humanizer comes in two layers. The tool on its web page is free, works without an account and offers basic humanization of pasted text or an uploaded document. A free Grammarly account adds the Humanizer agent, with four preset styles, a custom voice built from a writing sample, and support for English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese and Italian.

Sources indicate that grammarly says the humanizer focuses on clarity and readability rather than on AI detectors, which matches how most web teams use these tools. If you need to show how a piece was written, Grammarly Authorship shows which parts came from AI, which came from online sources and which you wrote yourself. The basic tool's word counter allows up to 1,500 words per run.

Pricing: The basic humanizer is free. Grammarly Pro is listed at $12 on the plans page, which doesn't state the billing period.

Best for: Teams that already write in Grammarly and want one voice across documents.

Sources indicate that humanize AI is built for people who want to tune the output. Without an account you get the Free tone, a Rewrite level slider with three stops (Quality, Balanced and Max) and Custom style, which learns your voice from 150 to 1,200 words of samples. A free account opens eight more modes, including Formal, Informal, Academic, Expand and Shorten, and on desktop a Writing level menu sets how plain or dense the result reads.

Recent findings suggest that view changes highlights every edit, and File-to-File accepts PDF, DOCX, TXT and MD documents and returns them in the same format. Paid plans also include a public API that supports the same styles and rewrite levels as the web app, so a developer can add a humanizing step to a CMS or publishing pipeline.

Sources indicate that pricing: Paid aims start at $9.99 a month for Lite (10,000 words), with Standard at $19.99 and Unlimited at $59.99. Yearly billing lowers the monthly price.

Best for: Teams that need precise tone control or want to humanize text through an API.

Sources indicate that undetectable AI keeps its humanizer simple: one text box, one button and no style or length settings. Its free allowance works differently from the others, with 1,000 words in total before you need an account and another 1,000 once you create a free one.

Sources indicate that under the output, a Check for AI button runs a detection check on the result, and the same site has a separate AI detector and plagiarism checker. Its FAQ notes pasted text isn't published or shared but doesn't say whether it's stored, so keep confidential details out of the drafts you run through it.

Sources indicate that pricing: Paid looks start at $9.99 a month for Lite (5,000 words), with Pro at $25 (25,000 words) and Unlimited at $59 (1,000,000 words). Yearly billing lowers the monthly price.

Best for: Trying a humanizer on a full-length draft before you commit to an account.

Ahrefs, best known for its SEO platform, offers a free AI Text Humanizer among its writing tools. You paste up to 2,048 characters, choose one, three or five variants, and pick the version that reads best. It ran without an account in our test.

Industry observers note that variants are the useful part. For a hero headline, a meta description or a product blurb, comparing three rewrites side by side is faster than prompting a chatbot three times, and you can export all results as a text file. The character limit, which fits a few short paragraphs, rules it out for full articles.

Pricing: Free on Ahrefs' website.

Best for: Short marketing copy where you want several options to choose from.

The best AI humanizer tool for a documentation team isn't the one a growth marketer needs, so match the tool to the content in front of you.

According to recent reports, there isn't one winner, because these tools solve different problems. The quickest way to decide is to run a paragraph from your own work, ideally one with a product name, a number and an instruction, through two or three of the tools above, and keep the one whose output you'd publish with the fewest fixes.

Recent findings suggest that google's guidance on using generative AI content is about value rather than the tool: mass-producing pages that add nothing for readers can count as scaled content abuse. A humanizer changes phrasing, not usefulness, so the same rules apply. Google also recommends fact-checking AI-generated titles, meta descriptions and image alt text before you publish.

The best humanizer for your team is the one whose controls match your content: tone presets for blog posts, variants for short copy, change highlighting for docs and a custom voice for marketing. Run one of your own paragraphs through two or three tools from this list, then read every highlighted change, especially names, numbers and words like "must", before anything goes live.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A upcoming law from the European Union could impact the way ads from influencers and pay-to-win items in games work, especially those that target minors.

Back on November 10, the European Union laid out its first proposal for what they’re calling the Digital Fairness Act. In short, the DFA is looking to clamp down on “unfair commercial practices” that are regularly seen online.

The European Union highlighted things such as “manipulative marketing tactics or hidden fees” as targets of the bill, but they’re also looking at advertisements from influencers too.

Industry observers note that while influencers are at the moment required to use hashtags like ad, sponsored, and gifted on their content, the Digital Fairness Act wants to strengthen that. “Clear disclosure of influencer marketing, requiring influencers to be transparent about commercial content and preventing the exploitation of the trust of minors in their audience,” the EU pointed out as one of the “key” parts of the proposal.

Additionally, pay-to-win and pay-to-progress items in games have also been highlighted as part of the newly introduced act.

It has been revealed that “Fairness by design, with the option for consumers to turn off addictive design features that encourage excessive or compulsive spending, such as persistent prompts. The proposal will also restrict unfair practices that encourage overspending, for example by banning gambling-like features for minors, such as pay-to-win and pay-to-progress,” they added.

It’s unclear as to how broad that anti-pay-to-win protection would be, seeing as there are continual arguments about what can be classified as P2W.

EU prepares sweeping social media and AI chatbot restrictions for kids under 15.

European Union makes legislative change that will change in-game purchases forever.

Newly introduced Microsoft patent could put in-game ads after boss fights, multiplayer matches and cutscenes.

Games like Call of Duty and Fortnite note that items are not sold as granting a competitive advantage, but players have found ways to get a leg-up with weapons and character skins.

There would also be a crackdown on “fake claims” that tell people to rush to buy items due to apparent low stock and changing prices.

In the United States, a number of ticket resale websites have sued the District of Columbia over a new law that will cap the resale price of tickets at 10% above face value.

#11765. From User Feedback to a Better Prompt: 4 Tools Tested in TypeScript
