Scientists discovered the brain doesn't make decisions the way we thought

📅 13 Jul 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (810 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that scientists at the University of Illinois Urbana Champaign have uncovered evidence that could reshape how researchers think about both the brain and artificial intelligence.
  • Led by electrical and computer engineering professor Yurii Vlasov at The Grainger College of Engineering, the research was published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Science (PNAS).
  • The human brain is widely regarded as the most complex structure in the known universe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that scientists at the University of Illinois Urbana Champaign have uncovered evidence that could reshape how researchers think about both the brain and artificial intelligence. Their findings suggest that decision making begins much earlier in the brain than traditional theories propose, offering fresh ideas for designing future AI systems that are more capable and far more energy efficient.

Led by electrical and computer engineering professor Yurii Vlasov at The Grainger College of Engineering, the research was published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Science (PNAS). The study points to an unexpected role for early sensory brain regions in decision making, challenging the long accepted view that decisions emerge only after information moves through a strict hierarchy of brain regions.

Rethinking How the Brain Makes Decisions.

The human brain is widely regarded as the most complex structure in the known universe. Scientists still do not fully understand how it works, which is why reverse engineering the brain was identified by the National Academy of Engineering in 2008 as one of the 14 grand challenges for engineering in the 21st century.

It has been revealed that for decades, many artificial intelligence systems, including convolutional neural networks, have been inspired by the idea that the brain processes information in a one way sequence. According to this traditional model, sensory information travels upward through increasingly complex brain regions until it reaches the frontal cortex, where decisions are made.

Vlasov and other researchers have increasingly questioned whether that picture is complete.

Instead, they are exploring a model based on natural intelligence, which has been refined through evolution over hundreds of millions of years. In this framework, the brain does not rely only on a step by step flow of information. Decision making also depends on interconnected feedback loops that allow information to move in both directions between brain regions.

Because biological intelligence performs remarkably complex tasks while using far less energy than today's AI systems, understanding this architecture could help guide the development of future artificial intelligence.

"We want to learn from a billion years of evolution," Vlasov said. "How is that biological intelligence organized architecturally? Can we learn from the architectural side of the brain and emulate that to make AI more effective, less power hungry, and more intelligent than it at the moment is? In the level of decision-making, that's where current AI is lacking.".

Early Brain Regions Show Decision Making Activity.

To investigate how these processes work, the research team focused on the brain's earliest stages of sensing and perception.

According to recent reports, the scientists recorded neural activity in mice as they navigated a virtual reality corridor and made perceptual decisions. They found evidence of decision related activity in the primary somatosensory cortex (S1), one of the brain's earliest sensory processing areas.

Rather than simply passing information forward, S1 appeared to be influenced by higher brain regions through feedback loops. This top down regulation suggests that decision making involves continuous communication across multiple brain areas instead of a simple one direction flow of information.

It has been revealed that "The neural code of the brain is still mostly an unknown language," Vlasov said. "But this systems-level understanding can be viewed as a potential impact on how more efficient artificial neural networks can be built -- how the next generation of AI can be thought through. Maybe with these analogies that we learn from real brains, we can improve AI further.".

What the Findings Could Mean for Future AI.

The researchers emphasize that the study does not provide a blueprint for building better artificial intelligence. Instead, it offers upcoming insights into how the brain organizes decision making that could eventually inspire future AI architectures.

Next, Vlasov and his team strategy to investigate the timing of these brain signals in greater detail. They also intend to develop upcoming technologies for measuring neural activity to better understand how feedback loops emerge and coordinate different levels of brain processing.

Recent findings suggest that "By looking at the fast temporal dynamics of neural activity, maybe we can understand better how these feedback loops are engaged in making decisions," Vlasov said. "Maybe that's the approach that potentially uncovers these presently unknown mechanisms -- how these feedback loops are organized dynamically and how they form and shape different levels of processing. Maybe that can be implemented in fresh architectures for AI.".

Materials provided by University of Illinois Grainger College of Engineering. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The day is finally here: Grand Theft Auto 6 is available to play worldwide.
  • I'm curious how many people stayed up until midnight in their region to give the game a go.
  • More broadly, I wonder about the impact GTA 6 will have on the wider world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The day is finally here: Grand Theft Auto 6 is available to play worldwide. It's destined to become the largest video game release of all time, and probably one of the biggest entertainment releases of all time. So we're doing a launch day live blog to chart its arrival in the world.

Have you played it yet? I'm curious how many people stayed up until midnight in their region to give the game a go. I couldn't manage it but my college-age son was contemplating it. And if you have played it, what do you think - what are your early impressions? Is this what you were waiting for?

More broadly, I wonder about the impact GTA 6 will have on the wider world. I've already seen nearly all mainstream news and media outlets attempt to cover the game - and many other kinds of businesses - so will GTA 6 make people reappraise video games?

It has been revealed that moreover, exactly how substantial will the launch be? The record books are ready to be written in, but what exactly will be written? And how will other games fare in GTA's wake - better, or worse? There's lots to consider as the ripples spread around the world.

We'll pull-in stories and developments, and your comments, as we chart the arrival of Rockstar's game around the world. Let's get to it.

Our live coverage of this event has finished.

An historic day in gaming and there's loads to unpack. But to begin with, this: did you take a day off to play GTA 6, and have you played it yet?

Rockstar's marketing department has gone all out.

The marketing push by Rockstar to have GTA 6 imprint on real-world cities has been impressive to see. There have been festivals in Miami, Selfridges dedicated a portion of its department store to selling GTA merch, but there's more than this besides. The London Standard summarised much of the activity in London in a video on Instagram.

A post shared by The Standard (@thelondonstandard).

Rockstar employment tribunal verdict could take weeks.

According to recent reports, the din of release is in danger of drowning out the Rockstar employment tribunal that came to a close this week in Scotland. Former Eurogamer video producer Chris Bratt - now co-owner of People Make Games - has been following the case closely, and reported yesterday that a verdict in the case could take "weeks".

Recent findings suggest that he quotes Judge Lucy Wiseman as saying: "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as quickly as I possibly can.".

Recent findings suggest that and that's it for the Rockstar tribunal! We await the judge's decision, but how long will it take? Judge Lucy Wiseman: "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as rapidly as I possibly can.".

Yesterday, we independently confirmed that most, if not all, of the fired Rockstar employees are credited in the GTA 6 credits - which are, according to Chris Tapsell, our reviewer, an enormous thing in their own right.

Here’s how significant it is, news-wise:.

Yesterday, my mother _(whose single dabble in gaming over the years can be described as,“working out the way to bypass the Brontosaurus Guarding Causeway in the text adventure Time Machine, is to GIVE it the Ship’s Biscuit found aboard the Marie Celeste”)_ texted me to ask if I was “ready for tomorrow?”.

I instantly assumed I’d made or hinted at some initiative to do something with her and subsequently forgotten.

BUT, NO. She was asking if I was ready for GTA. A product I have never mentioned in her presence in all my many years.

So if you’ve got the over-seventies non-gamers talking… I’d say you’ve cracked it.

Goodness! And will your mother also be playing it?

My inbox is flooded with all kinds of brands trying to get in on the GTA 6 hype.

The most recent one? Petrol prices. "Having to refuel your car in GTA 6 adds another layer of realism to the game, but it's something real-life drivers have to think about every time they get behind the wheel," stated Beth Fountain, fuel expert at somewhere called Interfuels.

"With petrol and diesel prices remaining high, filling up can take a significant chunk out of someone's monthly budget, particularly for those who rely on their vehicles for work or regular travel.

"While players might find the latest mechanic frustrating, it's a reminder of how much we depend on fuel in everyday life and how promptly those costs can add up.".

Sources indicate that there's another one from Just Eat, the food delivery firm, which has apparently made a real controller with Just Eat order button on it for you to order food while gaming. It's not specifically GTA 6-linked but it's jumping on that bandwagon. The controller is apparently synced to your Just Eat account. Imagine mashing that by accident and having an accidental feast turn up.

"When you're deep into a high-stakes gaming session nothing kills the moment faster than having to pause the action just to sort out food. With the Just ChEAT Button, Just Eat has unlocked the ultimate hack to evade the kitchen, enabling gamers to stay just where they are and locked into play," said Just East UK and Ireland marketing director Tina Koehler.

It's not clear where you can buy this controller or how much it costs. It's described as "limited edition". I wonder if that means only one has been made.

The goofy things people are already doing in GTA 6.

According to recent reports, many people are playing GTA 6 already of course and doing expectedly bizarre things in it. From lobbing hammers like Crocodile Dundee lobs cans of tinned food, to dropkicking people, to attempting to dive through a car window while oiled up and in one's pants - Connor has rounded up some of the goofiest clips around.

You are brilliant, Eurogamer readers!

I just want to resurface the winning entry to the GTA memories competition we ran at the tail-end of last week, because it's funny and uplifting, and I still smile about it.

My favourite GTA memory is introducing my nan to Vice City.

She'd never played a video game before, so I told her she could pretty much do whatever she wanted.

She spent the first 20 minutes driving around obeying traffic lights and apologising whenever she bumped into another car.

Then she accidentally punched someone.

I don't know what happened, but something just clicked.

Within half an hour she'd stolen a police car, run over several pedestrians and was shouting at the telly because the police wouldn’t leave her alone.

My grandad came in to see what all the noise was about.

Without even looking up she just noted, "I'm wanted for murder, Barry. Put the kettle on.".

Genuinely one of the funniest afternoons of my childhood.

I'm on the management team for a charity and they've scheduled their AGM for tonight at 6pm. Of all the dates! I've had to weigh up not doing my duty for selfish video game reasons.

It has been revealed that I must be growing up because I've decided that going to the AGM is the right thing to do and that GTA 6 probably isn't that good, anyway. Right?

Well! Allow the Eurogamer comments to decide. I think you should set GTA 6 up in another room in the building you're holding the AGM in, and find excuses during it to nip out and play. It'll be like a Mrs Doubtfire moment. Nothing can go wrong.

It has been revealed that another email from a shopping comparison site, Idealo, and this time about PS5 Pro demand, which has apparently leapt by 57 percent week on week because of GTA 6. This, by the way, is exactly what the industry was hoping would happen - that GTA 6 would reinvigorate console sales, which were slumping, not least because of their unprecedented rising prices. Apparently the price of PS5 consoles is rising in step with this demand.

"Grand Theft Auto debuts are major cultural moments, and GTA 6 is already having a noticeable impact on the wider gaming market, particularly when it comes to console demand," Katy Phillips from Idealo stated.

According to recent reports, "We're seeing a significant increase in interest in the PS5 Pro, with demand jumping by 57 percent in the week leading up to launch. At the same time, the price of the console has climbed by more than £450 since the end of October.".

GTA 6 videos you might find helpful.

IGN has produced a bunch of good Grand Theft Auto 6 videos I'm surfacing here in case you've missed them. There are a few performance-related videos of the game running on PlayStation and Xbox hardware:.

There's also footage of the first 15 minutes of the first mission:.

And some scuba diving and treasure hunting:.

GTA 6 is Metacritic's highest rated game ever.

A notable moment yesterday was GTA 6 being crowned as the highest-rated game ever on review-averaging site Metacritic. The game at the moment holds a 99 score there, averaged from 156 critics' reviews. The previous champion was the original Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, from 1998, with the same 99 average critics score. Will it retain the title as the days and weeks unfold?

Recent findings suggest that chris' expansive GTA 6 review is of course one of those contributing to that score. "A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

More ridiculous GTA 6 launch piggybacking and this time it's an email with a therapist talking about how the game might help teens with their dating outlooks.

States Natalie Buchwald, therapist and founder of Manhattan Mental Health Counseling:.

Sources indicate that "Psychologists sometimes talk about 'relationship scripts': the unspoken expectations we absorb about how relationships work, what partners owe each other and what success looks like. We pick these up long before we have much experience of our own, from family, friends, online spaces and the stories we see in entertainment.

Recent findings suggest that "No single film, game or influencer shapes someone's values on its own. What matters more is the overall mix of messages a person encounters, and whether they have the space to question them. That's particularly relevant now that dating advice is so widely available online, where some content frames relationships around status, control or getting something in return, rather than mutual respect.

"That's why the most useful thing parents can do isn't to hand over a set of rules. It's to help young people think critically about the scripts they're picking up. Being curious rather than critical, and asking what they've seen, what they think of it and what they believe makes a good partner, tends to keep conversations open.

Industry observers note that "Entertainment can play a helpful role here. A story built around a partnership, like Jason and Lucia's, can give parents a natural, low pressure starting point for conversations that might otherwise feel awkward.".

Industry observers note that chris referenced some of this in his review, praising Jason's tender and caring side, and his not being a toxic asshole. GTA 6 is also the first game to not only feature a couple but a female playable lead, having very much revolved around male fantasies in the past.

You can't use cheat in GTA 6 until you finish the main story.

Industry observers note that A reminder that cheats aren't usable in Grand Theft Auto 6 until you've finished the main story. Chris confirmed this yesterday, and offered details about cheats do work in the game when you've unlocked them.

More brand opportunism, this time optician Specsavers, and at least this one has a novel approach: a spoof partnership with a GTA company that has nothing to do with Grand Theft Auto.

Specsavers is circulating a very budget-looking partnership with a trucking tech giant called GTA Transport. It's billed as a "mix-up" in an email, but it's all far too staged and knowing to really be one.

Sources indicate that "It might not be the GTA partnership I originally had in mind but a deal's a deal," said Specsavers marketing person Neil Liddle. "I'm pleased to offer every driver at GTA Transport a free eye test.".

Industry observers note that bugz Singh at GTA Transport mentioned: "We were surprised when Specsavers got in touch, but we're delighted to be the GTA they've teamed up with. Our drivers spend all day on the road, so they're looking forward to their eye tests.".

The visuals are just something else. Even at this early stage, the story has already got me interested and invested in Jason and Lucia. And to top it all off, when I first started messing around with the car radio, ‘Master of Puppets’ was playing.

The second thing is that like all gtas is serves a reminder of what a hellscape urban America is. I’ve never been to the keys, but what looks like it should be a lovely set of islands is of course mostly a massive highway.

According to recent reports, ...long story short, what was intended to be a 1 hour go on a school night ended up being 3 hours and I slept through my alarm and am working from home today! I'll be playing this and pretty much only this for the next month or 2, no doubt...haven't been gripped by a game since Clair Obscure...nice to have that feeling back!

Some nice accounts of playing the game so far. Keep 'em coming!

GTA 6 developers fear for their jobs now the game has shipped.

Industry observers note that rockstar and Take-Two stand to make billions of dollars from GTA 6, but there's an enormous workforce - 4,711 people at last count - working at the GTA studio. Will they keep their jobs now the game has come out? That staff-count more than doubled after Red Dead Redemption 2 was released but will it grow again now?

Fears of lay-offs reach top volume both as the game is released and as Rockstar workers vote wheter to formally recognise a workers union there - a union that's proved so problematic in the past. Sherif has the full story below.

GameStop boss slams 'code in a box' trend in wake of GTA 6's discless release.

The boss of game-related retailer GameStop has spoken out about the trend of 'code in a box' game releases. This, of course, is pertinent this week with the discless release of GTA 6.

According to recent reports, "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend," GameStop boss Ryan Cohen told Bloomberg. "Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it's also hurt GameStop." Dom has the full story:.

It has been revealed that I have always wondered if one of the reasons I bounced off 5 was that I got it a long while down the line. (Also... I really didn't like the main characters).

Decided to be part of this "global media event" and bought it last night.

The intro is pretty gripping story wise, with a decent twist that somehow was kept completely under wraps.

According to recent reports, driving takes some getting used to, but the use of adaptive triggers on PS5 is great for this making cruising fairly easy. The traffic density and “smaller” roads really make getting about the city nicely realistically annoying. Spending more time cruising than normal for a GTA.

Being quoted is the risk one runs!

The spoof websites aren't in GTA 6 because Rockstar didn't think they were "necessary".

The spoof websites of previous GTA games don't make it into GTA 6. Apparently Rockstar didn't deem them "necessary". Let me tell you, as someone who writes for a website, that cuts deep.

Deus Ex legend Warren Spector has strong words for Rockstar about GTA 6.

Deus Ex legend Warren Spector, who was also involved in the making of influential series like Thief, System Shock and Ultima Underworld, has a few strong words to say about GTA 6. Or rather not GTA 6 itself but the colossal workforce, budget and development time Rockstar had to make i with.

"A billion dollars pays for a lot of games and a lot of salaries," Spector remarked. "Personally I'd rather have hundreds of games and full employment than one game no matter how amazing it is.".

In a recent development, I'm genuinely surprised that some gaming companies are ernestly trying to release and market their games today of all days - even this week. Did you want to know about a Goat Simulator 3 expansion that arrived today, called Dizzyworld? Well, now you do. And it's by far the only game I'm being sent press releases about.

My favourite press release about a game unrelated to GTA 6 - though it sounds like a parody that could be in the game - is one that made me do a double-take. "Sperm Adventure 'Become' Delayed to First Half of 2027," it read. The entire press release is packed with innuendo. And it's - judging by its Steam page - a real thing. Will you "embark on life's greatest tiny journey"?

GTA 6 is dominating Twitch viewer figures in a big way.

Industry observers note that back to GTA 6, and the impact of this game's arrival can be seen clearly on Twitch viewership numbers at the moment. GTA 6 is by far the most watched category on the streaming platform, with more than 1.6 million viewers. The next highest category is the broad "just chatting" category 2ith 330k viewers, followed by World of Warcraft with 72k viewers.

For balance, presentation and intro to story/characters are great.

"Laser Disc vibes" is not a phrase I've heard before, but I like it and think I'll steal it.

All 34 of the fired Rockstar employees are in the GTA 6 credits.

Here's a curious development. With Rockstar publishing the full cast list for GTA 6, I've been more able to cross-check the names of the 34 fired employees against it. And, success, they do all appear in the credits. But six of them are not contained in the "former employees" section of the credits, where everyone else is, which is curious. I'm trying to find out what gives.

Jason Duval actor finally confirmed.

Incidentally, that full cast list also confirms - finally - who the actor is that plays Jason Duval in the game. And, yes, it's Dylan Rourke, who everyone thought it was.

#11666. Alan Turing's biggest AI assumption may have been wrong

📅 14 Jul 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1187 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Alan Turing's biggest AI assumption may have been wrong

📅 14 Jul 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1187 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Alan Turing's famous ideas about artificial intelligence may have sent AI research down the wrong path for the past 75 years, according to prominent computer scientist Peter J.
  • Recent findings suggest that in his new book, Turing's Mistake: Escaping the Yoke of Unintelligent Machines, Denning argues that two foundational assumptions made by Turing in 1950 continue to shape AI research today.
  • Industry observers note that "These two claims have shaped much of AI research and development," Denning writes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alan Turing's famous ideas about artificial intelligence may have sent AI research down the wrong path for the past 75 years, according to prominent computer scientist Peter J. Denning.

Recent findings suggest that in his new book, Turing's Mistake: Escaping the Yoke of Unintelligent Machines, Denning argues that two foundational assumptions made by Turing in 1950 continue to shape AI research today. The first is that intelligence can exist independently of a physical body and therefore be recreated in computer software. The second is that a machine can demonstrate intelligence by successfully imitating a human in conversation, an idea that later became known as the Turing test.

Industry observers note that "These two claims have shaped much of AI research and development," Denning writes. "My premise is that our acquiescence to these claims has led to the AI mess in which we find ourselves today.".

Recent findings suggest that denning argues that pursuing artificial general intelligence (AGI), or machines with human level intelligence, is unlikely to succeed. Instead, he warns, the technologies society is building could introduce significant new risks.

At the heart of Denning's argument is the idea of tacit knowledge, the vast amount of human understanding that cannot easily be put into words or represented in a form that computers can process.

He claims machine learning cannot capture five major categories of tacit knowledge: common sense, everyday interactions with people and the environment, emotions and perception, practical performance skills, and the social and historical knowledge embedded in culture.

Researchers have long attempted to organize common sense into databases. One of the best known efforts was Douglas Lenat's Cyc project, which began in the 1980s with the goal of creating an extensive collection of common sense facts. After four decades of work, the project contained roughly 25 million entries.

In a recent development, "Yet even this treasury could not add up to a background of common sense sufficient to make expert systems smart enough to be experts," Denning notes. "Cyc validated that much of the knowledge that makes people experts cannot be articulated as propositions.".

Denning believes practical skills present an even greater challenge.

In a recent development, "Our performance skills in thousands of domains cannot be communicated to machines," he explains. "Whereas descriptions of skillful outcomes ('know what') can often be represented as bits and stored in a machine, we do not know how to encode the embodied knowledge for skillful performance ('know how').".

He points to accomplished musicians as an example.

"A virtuoso violinist can play beautiful music yet cannot describe to an acolyte how to produce it.

"Even if a robot could observe and imitate skilled humans, having no biological body, a robot cannot grasp how the musician feels when playing beautiful music or how an audience feels when hearing it.".

Denning also includes intuition, gut feelings, imagination, and spontaneous creativity among the forms of tacit knowledge that remain beyond the reach of machines.

Why Human Knowledge Resists Encoding.

Denning argues that all of these limitations stem from what he calls the "representation problem.".

Computers can only perform calculations using data and instructions that have been encoded into physical forms they can recognize and process. Tacit knowledge, however, does not naturally fit into that framework.

Recent findings suggest that "Behind every word is a deep well of tacit knowledge that gives it meaning," Denning says. "Words are but symbolic representations of meanings, not the meanings themselves. Commonly used Large Language Models, such as ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini only manipulate words, they cannot know or understand the meaning of what they are saying.".

According to Denning, this creates a fundamental divide. Because scientists still cannot fully explain how tacit knowledge works in humans, they also cannot translate it into a form machines can use.

"How we host tacit knowledge is largely a mystery," Denning admits. "All we know is that it is embodied. We have no idea what we might observe and measure in our bodies to reveal it.".

Context and Culture Shape Intelligence.

Denning also argues that intelligence depends heavily on context, the surrounding circumstances that give words, actions, and decisions their meaning.

Recent findings suggest that context allows people to recognize sarcasm, humor, sincerity, and emotion. It helps determine when to be diplomatic, when to joke, and how to interpret countless social cues.

Recent findings suggest that "When you inquire into where an assumption of the current context came from, you discover it rests on previous conversations from previous contexts. Each of those in turn rests on further previous conversations and their contexts. This pattern is endless and fractal," Denning explains.

Culture presents another major obstacle for AI.

Denning describes culture as encompassing values, norms, judgments, history, communities, moods, and even relationships involving power and care.

"Human conversations are imbued with background assumptions that give meaning and relevance to the words being used," Denning explains.

"Scaling up LLMs with ever larger neural networks will not enable them to acquire the embodied human knowledge we call culture. LLMs will not attain the objective of the Turing test: to demonstrate machine thought indistinguishable from human thought.".

AI Safety and the Limits of Human Understanding.

Denning concludes that humans and AI systems may ultimately develop different forms of tacit knowledge that neither can fully understand.

In a recent development, "Machines cannot read our tacit knowledge and we cannot read theirs," he writes. "We are aliens across an uncrossable divide.".

It has been revealed that he argues this gap raises serious concerns about AI safety. If machines cannot interpret the unspoken context behind human intentions, reliably aligning advanced AI systems with human goals may prove impossible.

"Through AI automation, agentic networks of machines are likely to develop their own machine intelligence that does not reach the level of human general intelligence but is still quite capable of creating severe problems for humans. This threat is a greater than a take-over by superintelligent machines," he explains.

According to recent reports, "Machine intelligence has different concerns from us and does not appear to care about us. Its ways of thinking and problem-solving look alien to us. We do not yet know how to live safely with these machines.

According to recent reports, "Pulling back from an AI automation singularity will demand much from us. We start by accepting that the familiar culture is fading away as intelligent machines appear in our society and we do not know what is coming. We decline to think like machines or be subservient to machines. We refuse to submit to a yoke imposed by low-intelligence machines. Most importantly, we reassert our humanity, declare once again what makes us different from machines, and celebrate those differences.".

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

It has been revealed that weekly. Free. One click to leave.

In a recent development, 7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

According to recent reports, we sent 1,000 streaming calls at the same moment through three self-hosted LLM gateways: the Langfuse AI Gateway, the LiteLLM proxy and AcruxCore. Each gateway was limited to 2 CPUs. As shipped, Langfuse finished 261 of the 1,000 streams and LiteLLM finished 403. Neither failure came from the gateway's own code.

Langfuse's failures came from Linux's open-file limit, which Docker sets to 1,024 by default. LiteLLM had that problem too, plus a second one: an empty key cache sent hundreds of database lookups at once, and the ones that waited longer than 10 seconds were rejected. This article reveals how each failure looked, how we traced it to its cause, and the settings that fixed it.

This benchmark measured the resource consumption of three LLM gateways under scaling concurrent streaming loads.

Full latency, memory, and feature results are available in the Langfuse vs LiteLLM vs AcruxCore benchmark.

In a recent development, first-token times are medians of the streams that succeeded. Up to 250 streams, every gateway succeeded. Then the errors started, and they did not look alike:.

It has been revealed that A 502 and a 503 point at different layers, so we expected two different causes. Two of the three turned out to share one cause.

According to recent reports, linux counts every network connection as an open file, and it caps how many open files one process may hold. The cap has two values. The soft limit is the cap that is in force now. The hard limit is the ceiling: a process may raise its own soft limit up to that value, and no further.

A streaming gateway holds two connections for each stream: one from the client, and one to the model provider. That makes about 1,000 open files at 500 streams, and about 2,000 at 1,000 streams. A gateway also needs a few more files for its database, its logs and its own libraries.

Docker on our machine gave every container a soft limit of 1,024 and a hard limit of 524,288. All three gateways received the same two numbers. What differed was how each program treats them when it starts:.

In a recent development, node.js raises its own soft limit to the hard limit at startup. The Rust and Python services keep 1,024, and neither project's Compose file sets a higher value. So the two gateways ran out of open files near 500 streams, which is the point where the errors started.

The out-of-files error appeared as a failed connection, not as a clear message. The Langfuse gateway's logs demonstrated failed connections to OpenAI, and also failed connections to Langfuse's own web service, which the gateway asks to check each key. Both come from one cause: a process that cannot open another file cannot open another socket. Its client then receives a 502.

According to recent reports, read the limit the process actually has, not the one you think Docker gave it. Process 1 is usually the main process in a container:.

It has been revealed that if the gateway runs under a supervisor or several workers, check each worker's process ID instead of process 1. To see how close a process is to its limit under load, count its open file descriptors:.

Sources indicate that raise the limit for the gateway service in its Compose file. We used 65,536 for all three gateways:.

It has been revealed that the same ulimits block works on the LiteLLM service. On Kubernetes or another platform, check /proc//limits inside a running container rather than assuming a value.

In a recent development, with the open-file limit raised, the Langfuse gateway finished all 1,000 streams. LiteLLM still returned 503 errors. To separate the two causes, we ran LiteLLM with one worker and only the open-file limit raised. All 500 streams succeeded in that ladder, but 595 of 1,000 failed with 503.

Sources indicate that the 503 message names the authentication database, so we read LiteLLM's logs and its source. The log gave the same reason for all 840 failed streams in these runs, 595 in that ladder and 245 in the cold-cache runs below:.

Three settings in LiteLLM explain it:.

When 500 calls arrive while the key is not in the cache, each call looks the key up in Postgres. All of those lookups queue for 10 connections. The worker was also using its whole CPU allowance at this point, which slows every query it sends and receives. We infer that this CPU load lengthens the queue, but we did not measure it separately. Whatever the share of each, the lookups at the back of the queue miss the 10-second deadline.

It has been revealed that if that explanation is right, the failures should depend on whether the key is already in the cache. So we ran 500 streams four more times. Three runs started after 75 seconds with no calls, which is longer than the 60-second cache. One run started right after a single warm-up call:.

The warm run had no failures. The cold runs failed by different amounts, 161, 84 and 0, because the result depends on how many lookups miss the deadline, and that changes from run to run. This probably explains why the earlier ladder succeeded at 500 and failed at 1,000. A run is a race between the lookup queue and the deadline, so a single ladder does not show where the limit is.

The warm-up result is the one we measured. Send one call with each virtual key after LiteLLM starts, and avoid quiet periods longer than 60 seconds before a traffic spike. A steady flow of traffic keeps the key in the cache.

According to recent reports, liteLLM also exposes three settings that act on this path. We did not test them, so treat them as places to look rather than proven fixes:.

According to recent reports, we raised the open-file limit to 65,536 for all three gateways and gave LiteLLM 2 workers, one per CPU, as its production guide recommends for a single machine. Then we ran the full ladder again:.

The open-file errors were gone for every gateway, and the Langfuse gateway gave the fastest first token of the three. LiteLLM still returned 120 × 503 at 500. That level started about 60 seconds after the first call of the ladder, so the cached key had probably just expired. All 1,000 succeeded at the next level, which started within 60 seconds of the 500 level.

Industry observers note that once nothing failed, CPU decided the first-token times. LiteLLM used its whole 2-CPU allowance from 100 streams on, and its median first token took 19.2 seconds at 1,000 streams. AcruxCore also used both CPUs from 100 streams on, and its first token at 1,000 streams was 3.8 s at the median and 9.7 s at p95. The Langfuse gateway peaked at 1.65 CPUs and 168 MiB, with a first token of 1.7 s at the median and 9.6 s at p95.

Each gateway also needs the rest of its stack, and that stack uses CPU too. While the Langfuse gateway served 500 streams, its whole stack used up to 3.1 CPUs, because the web service checked keys and the worker and ClickHouse stored usage. AcruxCore's whole stack peaked at 4.0 CPUs, because its API writes a trace for every call to Postgres. Size the stack around the gateway, not only the gateway container.

Industry News: Upcoming programmable photonic chip can control how fast light moves

📅 22 Jul 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1410 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers at Seoul National University and the University of Seoul have developed a programmable photonic integrated circuit that can slow light whenever needed.
  • The team was led by Professors Namkyoo Park and Sunkyu Yu of the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Seoul National University, working with Professor Xianji Piao of the School of Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of Seoul.
  • Slowing Light Could Help Solve a Computing Bottleneck.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers at Seoul National University and the University of Seoul have developed a programmable photonic integrated circuit that can slow light whenever needed.

The team was led by Professors Namkyoo Park and Sunkyu Yu of the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Seoul National University, working with Professor Xianji Piao of the School of Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of Seoul.

Slowing Light Could Help Solve a Computing Bottleneck.

It has been revealed that the rapid growth of generative AI and large scale AI models has sharply increased the amount of computing power required by data centers and servers. Conventional electronic semiconductors are struggling to keep pace because they consume large amounts of energy and face limits in how quickly they can transmit data.

These challenges have intensified interest in optical computing, which uses light rather than electrical signals to process information. Optical systems could potentially move data at extremely high speeds while using less power.

However, light also presents a major challenge. Because it naturally moves at a fixed speed, it is difficult to delay optical signals or temporarily hold them in place. Those capabilities are essential for creating buffers and memory functions in optical computers.

To address this problem, the researchers designed a programmable photonic circuit that can control both the speed and shape of optical signals. Their approach provides more flexibility over "slow light" than previously proposed methods.

The study was published in the renowned international journal Advanced Science.

Why Optical Signals Sometimes Need To Wait.

Photonic integrated circuits are emerging as a promising technology for processing information quickly and efficiently with light. In data centers, optical communication networks, and future computing systems, moving signals rapidly is only part of the challenge.

Industry observers note that systems must also ensure that different signals arrive at the correct time. In some cases, a light signal must be delayed so it can remain synchronized with other information moving through the system.

One method for creating these delays relies on coupled-resonator-induced transparency (CRIT), which uses interference among several optical resonators.

CRIT allows light within a selected frequency range to pass through a device while also reducing the speed at which the optical signal travels.

Fixed Optical Devices Limit Flexibility.

Sources indicate that traditional CRIT devices usually have operating characteristics that become permanent once they are manufactured. This makes it difficult to change how they function after fabrication.

For example, engineers who want to create a longer signal delay or work with a different frequency range often need to design and manufacture an entirely new photonic device.

That lack of adaptability increases the complexity of optical communication hardware and data center infrastructure. It can also raise costs and extend development schedules whenever fresh capabilities are needed.

It has been revealed that the problem is especially notable for AI servers and next-generation data centers, where enormous amounts of information must be processed in real time. Fixed optical components have therefore remained a major obstacle to more practical optical computing systems.

A Programmable Design for Controlling Light.

Sources indicate that the research team developed a different strategy by treating two optical states in CRIT systems, known as the bright mode and dark mode, as one unified degree of freedom. The researchers also added two controllable loop couplers.

In a recent development, together, these changes created a newly introduced design principle for programmable photonic integrated circuits. Resonator arrangements that were previously locked into one configuration after fabrication could instead be adjusted for different purposes.

Recent findings suggest that using the latest CRIT structure, the researchers showed that the movement of light could be delayed and controlled as needed. They also demonstrated that interference between the bright and dark modes could be handled as a single integrated design parameter.

This approach greatly expanded the flexibility of photonic resonator circuits that had previously been limited by fixed designs.

Controlling Delay, Bandwidth, and Signal Shape.

In a recent development, the researchers theoretically demonstrated that the two loop couplers could be used to adjust the bandwidth and shape of the passband. They could also control how long signals were delayed and how efficiently those signals traveled through the circuit.

This means that both the speed and transmission behavior of optical signals could be reconfigured across entire systems containing multiple resonators, rather than only within a single resonator.

Numerical simulations also revealed that the speed of optical pulses could be adjusted dynamically while the circuit was operating.

In a recent development, the results indicated that signal delay times could be changed without reducing processing performance. The system could also convert the frequency of light without requiring additional specialized components.

Simulations Suggest the Chip Could Be Practical.

The researchers used three-dimensional electromagnetic simulations to test whether the CRIT device could be built on a silicon nitride (Si3N4) photonic integrated circuit platform.

According to recent reports, they also evaluated a range of real-world concerns that could affect the device during manufacturing and operation. These included material losses, differences in resonator quality, backscattering, coupling fluctuations, phase errors in the loop couplers, and thermal crosstalk.

The simulations indicated that the proposed structure could continue to operate reliably under realistic conditions.

One Chip Could Perform Several Optical Functions.

The study introduces a programmable photonic platform that can control both the timing and frequency properties of light signals in real time.

The design could overcome the limitations of conventional optical delay devices, which typically perform only fixed functions. It also suggests that several key capabilities could eventually be combined within one photonic circuit.

These functions include signal synchronization, adjustable delay lines, optical buffers, and frequency conversion.

Industry observers note that the same design principles may also be useful beyond CRIT systems. The researchers believe the approach could be applied to a broad range of photonic circuits based on resonators, potentially providing a foundation for more adaptable optical signal processing technologies.

Potential Benefits for AI and Data Centers.

If the technology is commercialized, a single programmable optical chip could perform several tasks, including controlling signal speed and switching between different functions.

In that sense, the chip could operate in a way similar to a software-defined system, with its behavior adjusted according to changing needs.

This flexibility could help data centers and AI servers process information more efficiently while reducing energy consumption.

Combining several signal processing functions on one chip could also make optical communication equipment and sensor systems smaller and less expensive.

Over the longer term, the technology could support industries that depend on extremely fast information processing, including autonomous driving, next-generation communications, and quantum technologies.

Researchers Proposal Larger Programmable Photonic Systems.

Professor Namkyoo Park, co-corresponding author of the study from Seoul National University, stated, "This research is significant in that it proposes a newly introduced design principle that allows the flow of light within photonic integrated circuits to be reconfigured as needed, greatly enhancing design flexibility. We blueprint to expand this technology toward large-scale programmable photonic integrated circuits based on silicon photonics and photonic AI technologies.".

Co-first authors Dr. Seungkyun Park and Ph.D. student Beomjoon Chae, who led the theoretical framework and numerical analysis, added, "Through this study, we realized that reinterpreting conventional photonic resonator physics from a different perspective can serve as a starting point for discovering upcoming functionalities in photonic integrated circuits. We plan to further develop this research toward practical device implementation and experimental validation.".

In a recent development, dr. Seungkyun Park is affiliated with the InnoCORE PICORE Center at KAIST and is at the moment conducting research on photonic AI and quantum optics at the Photonic Systems Laboratory, Seoul National University.

Ph.D. student Beomjoon Chae is conducting research on programmable photonic integrated circuits at the Intelligent Wave Systems Laboratory, SNU.

The research received support from the Ministry of Science and ICT through the Innovative Research Center (IRC) program, the Basic Research Laboratory (BRL) program, and the Young Researcher Program.

Dr. Seungkyun Park also participated in the study with support from the InnoCORE program (PICORE Center).
